Plain-English Definition: A tax-free swap of one life insurance or annuity policy for another under IRS Section 1035.
Example: You exchange an old annuity for a new one without paying tax.

Plain-English Definition: A federal tax test that checks whether premiums in the first seven years exceed limits, which would make a policy a MEC.
Example: Premiums above the 7-pay limit trigger MEC status.

Plain-English Definition: A Verisk database report of past property and auto claims, similar to CLUE.
Example: An underwriter checks A-PLUS for prior losses.

Plain-English Definition: An advisory organization, owned by member insurers, that provides standard forms and loss costs, similar to ISO.
Example: A mutual insurer uses AAIS farm forms.

Plain-English Definition: Latin for 'from the beginning'. A policy void ab initio is treated as if it never existed.
Example: A policy obtained by fraud is rescinded ab initio and the premium refunded.

Plain-English Definition: Giving up ownership of damaged property to the insurer in exchange for a total loss payment.
Example: A shipowner abandons a wrecked vessel to the insurers.
US Notes: Property policies usually say the insured cannot abandon property to the insurer.

Plain-English Definition: A rider that lets you receive part of the death benefit early if you are terminally, chronically or critically ill.
Example: You receive 50% of the benefit after a terminal diagnosis.

Plain-English Definition: Using data and algorithms to approve some life applicants without a medical exam.
Example: A healthy 30-year-old is approved in minutes without blood tests.

Plain-English Definition: A sudden, unexpected and unintended event that causes injury or damage.
Example: Slipping on ice and breaking an arm is an accident.

Plain-English Definition: A feature where your first at-fault accident doesn't raise your premium.
Example: No surcharge after your first fender-bender.
US Notes: Banned in some states such as California.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance paying set amounts for injuries from accidents, such as fractures or ER visits.
Example: $500 for a broken arm.

Plain-English Definition: Grouping of losses by the year the accident happened.
Example: All losses from accidents in 2024 belong to AY 2024.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance paying if you die or lose a limb, eyesight or hearing in an accident.
Example: AD&D pays 50% of the benefit for loss of one hand.

Plain-English Definition: A rider that pays an extra benefit if death results from an accident.
Example: An extra $250,000 paid for accidental death.

Plain-English Definition: The build-up of many insured risks exposed to the same event.
Example: Too many insured homes in one coastal county.

Plain-English Definition: The period when money in a deferred annuity grows before payouts start.
Example: Contributions grow tax-deferred in the accumulation phase.

Also Known As: Association for Cooperative Operations Research and Development
Plain-English Definition: A nonprofit that sets data standards (XML, JSON, forms) for exchanging insurance information.
Example: Agency software sends ACORD XML to a carrier.

Plain-English Definition: An older ACORD standard file format used to download policy data from carriers to agency systems.
Example: A carrier sends daily AL3 downloads to agents.

Plain-English Definition: Standardized application and certificate forms used across the US industry, such as ACORD 25 (certificate of liability insurance) and ACORD 125.
Example: A broker fills out ACORD 125 and 126 for a commercial GL submission.

Plain-English Definition: Costs of getting new business, such as commissions, marketing and underwriting.
Example: Commissions and premium taxes are acquisition costs.

Plain-English Definition: A natural event outside human control, such as a flood, earthquake or lightning.
Example: Lightning striking a barn is an act of God.

Plain-English Definition: Basic self-care tasks, usually bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, continence and transferring, used to trigger long-term care benefits.
Example: Needing help with two ADLs qualifies you for LTC benefits.

Plain-English Definition: The value of property at the time of loss: replacement cost minus depreciation.
Example: A 5-year-old TV that costs $1,000 new may be worth $400 ACV.
US Notes: Some states define ACV by statute or case law, including whether labor can be depreciated.

Plain-English Definition: A farmer's historical average yields, used to set crop insurance guarantees.
Example: A 10-year APH of 180 bushels per acre.

Plain-English Definition: The percentage of total average costs for covered benefits that a plan pays.
Example: A silver plan has about 70% actuarial value.

Plain-English Definition: A professional who uses math and statistics to price insurance, set reserves and measure risk.
Example: An actuary calculates how much to charge 30-year-old non-smokers for term life.
US Notes: Credentialed by the CAS (property/casualty) or SOA (life/health).

Plain-English Definition: A person or company added to someone else's policy so they are also protected, often required by a contract.
Example: A landlord requires a tenant's liability policy to list the landlord as an additional insured.

Plain-English Definition: The increase in living costs, such as rent and meals, after a covered loss forces you out of your home.
Example: Paying $2,000/month rent while your home is rebuilt.

Plain-English Definition: Extra premium charged because of a mid-term change that increases the risk.
Example: Adding a pool to your home policy costs $80 additional premium.

Plain-English Definition: An arrangement where an insurer or TPA processes claims for a self-funded plan but doesn't take the risk.
Example: A big insurer handles claims for an employer's plan under an ASO contract.

Plain-English Definition: An insurer licensed by a state to do business there, subject to its rate and form rules and covered by its guaranty fund.
Example: Most personal auto insurers are admitted.

Plain-English Definition: A notice explaining that a consumer report influenced a decision to decline or charge more.
Example: A letter says your insurance score affected your premium.

Plain-English Definition: Reinsurance that pays if reserves for past claims turn out to be too low.
Example: Covers reserve growth above $500M on old liability claims.

Plain-English Definition: When people who are more likely to have a loss are more likely to buy insurance, making the pool riskier.
Example: People who know they need surgery sign up for health insurance right before.

Plain-English Definition: Satellite or aircraft images used to assess roofs, trees and hazards without visiting.
Example: An insurer spots a damaged roof from imagery.
US Notes: Some states restrict non-renewals based solely on aerial images.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance sold to members of an organization, like alumni or professional associations, often at group rates.
Example: A bar association sponsors a professional liability program.

Plain-English Definition: A 2010 federal law that reformed US health insurance, including marketplaces, subsidies, essential benefits and bans on pre-existing condition exclusions.
Example: You can't be denied a plan because of diabetes.

Plain-English Definition: Two ways insurers define age: the age at your nearest birthday, or at your last birthday.
Example: At 35 and 7 months you're 36 ANB but 35 ALB.

Plain-English Definition: The agent bills and collects premium from the client, then pays the insurer net of commission.
Example: A commercial client pays the agency, not the carrier.

Plain-English Definition: Software agencies use to manage clients, policies, commissions and documents.
Example: An agency uses Applied Epic or Vertafore AMS360.

Plain-English Definition: A licensed person or firm who sells insurance on behalf of one or more insurers.
Example: A local State Farm agent sells you home and auto insurance.
US Notes: Agents must hold a state license for each line and state.

Plain-English Definition: Professional liability coverage for insurance agents against claims of mistakes in placing coverage.
Example: A client sues an agent who forgot to add flood coverage.

Plain-English Definition: Reinsurance that pays when total losses for a year exceed a set amount or loss ratio.
Example: Pays when the crop portfolio's loss ratio exceeds 110%.

Plain-English Definition: The most the insurer will pay for all claims combined during one policy period.
Example: A business has a $2M aggregate; after paying $2M in claims this year, no more claims are paid until renewal.

Plain-English Definition: Stop-loss that pays when the total claims for the whole group exceed a set amount.
Example: Pays when total claims exceed 125% of expected.

Plain-English Definition: A website that collects quotes from many insurers for comparison.
Example: A site shows 10 auto quotes side by side.

Plain-English Definition: A value the insured and insurer agree on in advance, which is paid for a total loss without arguing about depreciation.
Example: A classic car is insured for an agreed value of $60,000.

Plain-English Definition: Covers injury to passengers and third parties caused by aircraft operations.
Example: A plane crash injures people on the ground.

Plain-English Definition: A contract where what each side gives may be very unequal and depends on an uncertain event.
Example: You pay $800 in premium and might receive $300,000 if your house burns down, or nothing.

Plain-English Definition: Claim expenses that can be tied to a specific claim, such as defense lawyers and experts.
Example: $20,000 paid to a defense firm on one lawsuit is ALAE.
US Notes: NAIC statutory reporting uses the term DCC.

Plain-English Definition: The maximum amount a plan will pay for a covered service, often a negotiated rate with in-network providers.
Example: A doctor bills $300; the allowed amount is $180.

Plain-English Definition: Ways of managing or financing risk outside traditional insurance, such as captives, cat bonds and self-insurance.
Example: A company forms a captive to insure its own risks.

Plain-English Definition: A credit rating agency specializing in insurance companies.
Example: AM Best rates an insurer 'A+ (Superior)'.

Plain-English Definition: Policy wording that can reasonably be read in more than one way.
Example: 'Flood' might or might not include sewer backup; that is an ambiguity.

Plain-English Definition: The most a plan (commonly dental) will pay in a year.
Example: A dental plan's $1,500 annual maximum.
US Notes: ACA bans annual dollar limits on essential health benefits, but dental maximums remain for adults.

Plain-English Definition: Term insurance that renews each year with rising premiums as you age; YRT is also a common life reinsurance basis.
Example: Premium rises every year on a YRT policy.

Plain-English Definition: The detailed yearly financial report each insurer files with regulators using NAIC formats.
Example: The annual statement includes Schedule P for reserves.
US Notes: P&C statements are called the Yellow Book; life statements the Blue Book.

Plain-English Definition: The person whose life expectancy determines annuity payments; often also the owner.
Example: The annuitant is 65 and receives monthly income.

Plain-English Definition: Converting the annuity's value into a stream of regular payments.
Example: You annuitize at age 70 for life income.

Plain-English Definition: A contract with an insurer where you pay money in and receive regular income, often for life.
Example: You pay $100,000 and receive $550 a month for life.

Plain-English Definition: Wording that excludes a loss if an excluded cause contributed in any way, even if a covered cause also contributed.
Example: Flood damage is excluded even though wind also contributed.
US Notes: Not enforced in some states, such as California and Washington.

Plain-English Definition: Rules requiring insurers selling certain life and annuity products to detect and report money laundering.
Example: A large single premium paid in cash triggers review.
US Notes: Covered life insurers have AML program obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act.

Plain-English Definition: A disability definition that pays only if you can't do any job suited to your education and experience.
Example: After 2 years, LTD switches to any-occupation.

Plain-English Definition: A request asking your insurer to reconsider a denied claim or decision.
Example: You appeal a denied MRI with a letter from your doctor.

Plain-English Definition: The form you fill out to request insurance, giving information the insurer uses to decide and price.
Example: A life application asks about your health, hobbies and income.

Plain-English Definition: The actuary named by an insurer's board to give the regulator an opinion on the adequacy of its reserves.
Example: The appointed actuary signs the annual reserve opinion.

Plain-English Definition: Official authorization from an insurer for an agent to represent it, often filed with the state.
Example: An agent is appointed with five carriers.
US Notes: Most states require insurers to file appointments.

Plain-English Definition: A process for settling disagreements about the amount of a loss, using independent appraisers and an umpire.
Example: You and the insurer disagree on the roof repair cost, so each hires an appraiser.

Plain-English Definition: A clause requiring disputes to be settled by a private arbitrator instead of a court.
Example: A reinsurance dispute goes to a panel of three arbitrators.

Plain-English Definition: Long-tail liability claims from asbestos exposure and pollution that have cost insurers heavily for decades.
Example: An insurer increases A&E reserves.

Plain-English Definition: A residual market plan that assigns hard-to-insure drivers or employers to insurers.
Example: A high-risk driver is assigned to an insurer by the state plan.

Plain-English Definition: Transferring rights under a policy to someone else.
Example: A life policyowner assigns the policy to a bank as loan collateral.

Plain-English Definition: A document that lets a contractor or provider bill the insurer directly and pursue the claim.
Example: A water mitigation company has you sign an AOB and then bills your insurer.
US Notes: Florida restricted AOB for property claims in 2019 and 2022 after abuse; health providers routinely take AOB.

Plain-English Definition: Premium a reinsurer receives for risk it takes on from another insurer.
Example: A reinsurer books $10M assumed premium.

Plain-English Definition: The loss amount at which an excess or reinsurance layer starts to pay.
Example: An excess policy attaching at $10M pays once losses exceed $10M.

Plain-English Definition: The insured's current age, used for premiums that rise with age.
Example: Medigap attained-age pricing rises each year.

Plain-English Definition: The company that manages a reciprocal exchange on behalf of its members.
Example: Erie Indemnity is attorney-in-fact for Erie Insurance Exchange.

Plain-English Definition: A policy whose final premium is determined by an audit after it ends.
Example: Workers' comp and GL on payroll or sales basis are auditable.

Plain-English Definition: Automatic processing of claims by a system without human review.
Example: 90% of routine doctor visit claims are auto-adjudicated.

Plain-English Definition: Temporary coverage for newly acquired property until you report it to the insurer.
Example: A new car is covered for 14–30 days until you add it.

Plain-English Definition: A feature that automatically borrows from cash value to pay a missed premium to prevent lapse.
Example: A missed payment is covered by an APL.

Plain-English Definition: A clause, similar to coinsurance, that cuts claim payments proportionally when property is underinsured.
Example: Marine cargo underinsured by half receives half of the loss.
US Notes: Common in marine and London-market wordings used in the US.

Plain-English Definition: The expected yearly loss from catastrophes, averaged over many simulated years.
Example: A portfolio's hurricane AAL is $12M.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for aircraft hull damage and liability for passengers and third parties.
Example: An airline insures its fleet.

Plain-English Definition: Setting a life policy's date earlier than the application date to get a lower age-based premium.
Example: Backdating by 3 months to 'save age'.
US Notes: Most states limit backdating to 6 months.

Plain-English Definition: When an insurer unreasonably fails to meet its duties, such as denying or delaying a valid claim without good reason.
Example: An insurer ignores a reasonable settlement offer within limits, and the insured faces a large judgment.
US Notes: Bad faith law is state-specific; some states allow extra-contractual and punitive damages.

Plain-English Definition: A surety bond guaranteeing a defendant will appear in court.
Example: A bail agent posts bond for a defendant's release.
US Notes: Commercial bail is banned or largely eliminated in a few states, such as Illinois, Kentucky, Oregon and Wisconsin.

Plain-English Definition: When a provider bills you for the difference between their charge and the allowed amount.
Example: An out-of-network doctor bills you $120 above what your plan paid.

Plain-English Definition: Selling insurance through banks.
Example: A bank offers life insurance to mortgage customers.
US Notes: Less common in the US than elsewhere because of historic banking law limits, partly lifted by the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (1999).

Plain-English Definition: The starting rate before adjustments for the specific risk's features.
Example: A base rate for a territory is then adjusted for driver age and vehicle type.

Plain-English Definition: A property coverage form covering a short list of perils such as fire, lightning, windstorm, hail, explosion and vandalism.
Example: A vacant building insured on a basic form.

Plain-English Definition: The person or organization that receives the money when a claim is paid, especially from a life insurance policy.
Example: A husband names his wife as beneficiary of his life policy.

Plain-English Definition: How long benefits are paid, or (in Medicare) the span of a hospital or skilled nursing episode.
Example: An LTD benefit period to age 65.

Plain-English Definition: A deduction for when a repair makes property better than before the loss.
Example: New tires installed on a car with worn tires may carry a betterment charge.

Plain-English Definition: A bond guaranteeing that a winning bidder will sign the contract and provide performance and payment bonds.
Example: A contractor submits a bid bond with a public project bid.

Plain-English Definition: Software that manages invoicing, payment plans, collections and commissions for policies.
Example: The billing system issues a cancellation notice after missed payment.

Plain-English Definition: A temporary written agreement that coverage is in force until the policy is issued.
Example: A 30-day binder given to a mortgage lender at closing.
US Notes: State rules limit binder duration (often 90 days).

Plain-English Definition: Putting coverage into effect, often before the formal policy is issued.
Example: Your agent binds coverage at noon so you can drive the new car home.

Plain-English Definition: Permission given by an insurer to an agent or MGA to accept risks and issue coverage on its behalf.
Example: An MGA has authority to bind small restaurant policies.

Plain-English Definition: A COB rule: for a child covered by both parents' plans, the plan of the parent whose birthday comes first in the year pays first.
Example: Mom's birthday is March 5, Dad's is July 9, so Mom's plan is primary.

Plain-English Definition: One limit that applies across multiple locations or types of property instead of separate limits for each.
Example: A $10M blanket limit covering five warehouses.

Plain-English Definition: An endorsement that waives subrogation against anyone the insured agreed in a written contract to waive it for.
Example: A workers' comp policy includes a blanket waiver for all contract clients.

Plain-English Definition: Physical injury, sickness or disease to a person, including resulting death.
Example: A customer breaks a leg in your store.

Plain-English Definition: Pays for injuries you cause to other people.
Example: You cause a crash; BI pays the other driver's hospital bills.

Plain-English Definition: Latin for 'in good faith'; genuine and without fraud.
Example: A bona fide purchaser bought the car without knowing it was stolen.

Plain-English Definition: The set of policies written by an agent, broker or insurer.
Example: An agent's book of 3,000 home and auto policies.

Plain-English Definition: A regular report listing policies written or claims paid, sent from an MGA or cedent to an insurer or reinsurer.
Example: An MGA sends a monthly premium bordereau.

Plain-English Definition: A reserving method that blends expected losses with actual reported losses, useful for recent, immature years.
Example: BF is used for the latest accident year where data is thin.

Plain-English Definition: Costs to handle a data breach, like forensics, legal advice, notifying customers and credit monitoring.
Example: Notifying 50,000 customers after a hack.

Plain-English Definition: A property coverage form covering the basic perils plus extra ones like falling objects, weight of ice and snow, and water damage.
Example: An HO-2 policy is a broad form.

Plain-English Definition: A licensed intermediary who represents the buyer and places coverage with insurers.
Example: A large business uses a broker to build its insurance program.
US Notes: In many states 'broker' and 'agent' are both licensed as producers; the legal distinction varies.

Plain-English Definition: The broker officially authorized by the client to handle its account with an insurer.
Example: A client signs a BOR letter switching to a new broker.

Plain-English Definition: Covers buildings under construction against damage like fire, theft and wind.
Example: Covers a half-built apartment building damaged by fire.

Also Known As: IBNER; Incurred But Not Enough Reported
Plain-English Definition: A reserve for expected increases in claims already reported, beyond their case reserves.
Example: Adding $2M because case reserves on old claims tend to grow.

Plain-English Definition: A contract required by HIPAA when a vendor handles PHI for a health plan or provider.
Example: A cloud vendor signs a BAA with a health insurer.

Also Known As: Business Income; BI; Loss of Income
Plain-English Definition: Covers lost income and ongoing expenses when a business must close due to covered property damage.
Example: A restaurant closed 3 months after a fire gets lost profits paid.

Plain-English Definition: A package policy for small businesses combining property, liability and business income coverage.
Example: A small accounting firm buys a BOP.

Plain-English Definition: A contract for owners to buy a deceased owner's share of a business, often funded with life insurance.
Example: Partners each own a policy on the other.

Plain-English Definition: Grouping of financial transactions by the year they were recorded, regardless of when the policy or accident happened.
Example: Calendar year 2025 losses include reserve changes on older claims.

Plain-English Definition: A publicly managed, privately funded entity that sells residential earthquake insurance through participating insurers.
Example: You buy a CEA policy through your home insurer.

Plain-English Definition: Optional travel coverage letting you cancel for any reason, usually refunding 50–75% of costs.
Example: You decide not to go and recover 75%.

Plain-English Definition: Ending a policy before its expiration date, either by the policyholder or the insurer.
Example: You cancel your auto policy when you sell your car.
US Notes: States limit insurer cancellation after 60 days of a personal lines policy to reasons like non-payment or fraud.

Plain-English Definition: The part of the policy explaining how and when you or the insurer can cancel and how refunds work.
Example: The insurer must give 10 days' notice if cancelling for non-payment.
US Notes: State law sets minimum notice periods and allowed reasons for insurer cancellation.

Plain-English Definition: The maximum interest rate an indexed product can credit in a period.
Example: The index rose 15% but the cap limits credit to 10%.

Plain-English Definition: The amount of insurance an insurer or market is able and willing to write, limited by capital and appetite.
Example: After a big hurricane season, property capacity in Florida shrinks.

Plain-English Definition: Paying a provider a fixed amount per member per month regardless of how much care is used.
Example: A clinic gets $40 per member per month.

Plain-English Definition: An agent who sells for only one insurance company.
Example: An Allstate agent who sells only Allstate products.

Plain-English Definition: An insurance company owned by the business or group it insures.
Example: A hospital system forms a captive for its malpractice risk.
US Notes: Vermont, Utah, Delaware, North Carolina and others are popular domiciles; 831(b) micro-captives face IRS scrutiny.

Plain-English Definition: Covers goods in transit by sea, air or land.
Example: Coffee damaged by seawater during shipping.

Plain-English Definition: Changes in case reserves on known claims over time.
Example: Case reserves on 2022 claims rose 8% this year.

Plain-English Definition: The amount you get if you cancel a permanent policy, which is cash value minus surrender charges and loans.
Example: Surrendering pays $35,000 after a $5,000 surrender charge.

Plain-English Definition: The savings portion of a permanent life policy that grows over time and can be borrowed or withdrawn.
Example: After 20 years your whole life policy has $40,000 cash value.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance mainly concerned with legal liability for injuries and damage to others, plus workers' comp.
Example: GL, auto liability and workers' comp are casualty lines.

Plain-English Definition: A single event, such as a hurricane or earthquake, that causes very large losses for many policyholders at once.
Example: Hurricane Ian caused billions in insured losses.

Plain-English Definition: An adjuster who travels to disaster areas to handle large volumes of claims.
Example: CAT adjusters work storm claims for weeks after a hurricane.
US Notes: Many states issue emergency adjuster licenses after disasters.

Plain-English Definition: A bond that pays investors interest but loses principal if a specified disaster occurs, giving the issuer money to pay claims.
Example: Investors lose their principal after a qualifying California earthquake.

Plain-English Definition: Reinsurance protecting against the total of many losses from one catastrophe event.
Example: Pays hurricane losses above $100M up to $500M.

Plain-English Definition: Software that simulates thousands of possible disasters to estimate potential losses.
Example: A hurricane model estimates a 1-in-100-year loss of $500M.
US Notes: Florida reviews hurricane models through its Commission on Hurricane Loss Projection Methodology.

Plain-English Definition: A low-premium, very high-deductible ACA plan for people under 30 or with a hardship exemption.
Example: A 25-year-old buys a catastrophic plan.

Plain-English Definition: Latin for 'let the buyer beware'. It is the opposite of utmost good faith and does not apply to insurance.
Example: Unlike used car sales, insurance does not follow caveat emptor.

Plain-English Definition: The premium an insurer pays to its reinsurers.
Example: $10M ceded to reinsurers this year.

Plain-English Definition: A payment from the reinsurer to the ceding insurer to cover its acquisition costs on ceded business.
Example: A 30% ceding commission on a quota share.

Plain-English Definition: The insurer that transfers (cedes) part of its risk to a reinsurer.
Example: A regional insurer cedes 40% of its property risk.

Plain-English Definition: A document given to each member of a group plan describing their coverage under the master policy.
Example: You receive a certificate describing your group life benefit.

Plain-English Definition: A document proving a business has insurance, often required by clients or landlords. It does not change the policy.
Example: A contractor gives a COI to a homeowner before starting work.
US Notes: Several states restrict altering standard certificate forms.

Plain-English Definition: A non-US reinsurer approved by a state to post reduced collateral.
Example: A Bermuda reinsurer qualifies for reduced collateral.

Plain-English Definition: The part of a risk or premium passed to a reinsurer.
Example: Ceding 30% of each policy to the reinsurer.

Plain-English Definition: A reserving method that projects ultimate losses by applying historical development factors to current losses.
Example: Reserving actuaries run chain ladder on paid and incurred triangles.

Plain-English Definition: Taking back commission from an agent when a policy lapses or is cancelled early.
Example: An agent repays part of the commission after the policy lapses in month 4.

Plain-English Definition: Covers liabilities of those who charter (rent) a vessel.
Example: A charterer damages a ship by overloading it.

Plain-English Definition: A federal-state program providing low-cost health coverage for children in families that earn too much for Medicaid.
Example: A family's kids are covered by CHIP.

Plain-English Definition: A rider paying part of the death benefit if you can't perform two of six activities of daily living or have severe cognitive impairment.
Example: Dementia triggers monthly payments from the rider.

Plain-English Definition: Repeatedly replacing policies, often with the same insurer, mainly to generate new commissions.
Example: An agent replaces a client's annuity three times in five years.

Plain-English Definition: Florida's state-created, not-for-profit insurer of last resort for property.
Example: A Florida homeowner is placed with Citizens after private insurers leave.
US Notes: Similar state entities exist in Louisiana; Texas has TWIA for wind.

Plain-English Definition: Business income coverage when government orders block access to your premises due to nearby covered damage.
Example: Police close your street after a nearby explosion.

Plain-English Definition: A request to the insurer for payment under a policy after a loss, or a demand against an insured by someone they harmed.
Example: You file a claim for storm damage to your roof.

Plain-English Definition: Deciding how much of a health claim the plan will pay based on coverage, network and cost sharing.
Example: A $1,000 bill is adjudicated to a $600 allowed amount with $120 patient coinsurance.

Plain-English Definition: The insurer's decision not to pay a claim, with reasons.
Example: A flood claim is denied under a home policy's flood exclusion.
US Notes: States require written denial with reasons and time limits under unfair claims practices laws.

Plain-English Definition: Gathering facts, statements and evidence to determine whether and how much to pay on a claim.
Example: Collecting a police report and witness statements.

Plain-English Definition: A unique reference number assigned to a claim.
Example: Quote claim number 00-123456 when calling.

Plain-English Definition: The amount set aside by the insurer to pay a claim that is still open.
Example: The adjuster sets a $50,000 reserve on a bodily injury claim.

Plain-English Definition: The final agreement and payment that resolves a claim.
Example: You accept $12,000 to settle your car claim.

Plain-English Definition: The person or organization making a claim.
Example: A pedestrian hit by your car is the claimant on your liability claim.

Plain-English Definition: A person who investigates a claim, determines coverage and decides how much to pay.
Example: An adjuster inspects your hail-damaged roof.
US Notes: Adjusters must be licensed in most states.

Plain-English Definition: Money lost through inefficient claims handling, such as overpayment or missed recoveries.
Example: Failing to pursue subrogation causes leakage.

Plain-English Definition: Software that manages claims from first notice through payment and closure.
Example: Guidewire ClaimCenter tracks reserves and payments.

Plain-English Definition: A policy that covers claims first made against you during the policy period, for incidents after the retroactive date.
Example: A lawyer's malpractice policy responds to a suit filed this year about work done two years ago.

Plain-English Definition: A code describing a business's type of work, used to set rates for workers' comp and GL.
Example: Class 8810 (clerical) has a much lower rate than roofing.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for collector vehicles, often on an agreed value basis with mileage limits.
Example: A 1967 Mustang insured for $55,000 agreed value.

Plain-English Definition: A health claim that has all the information needed and can be processed without more investigation.
Example: A correctly coded claim with patient and provider IDs.

Applies To Lines: Property, Casualty/Liability, Commercial, Specialty, Financial Lines
Plain-English Definition: Checking whether an insurer has already received a submission for the same client from another broker.
Example: The system flags a duplicate submission and blocks the second broker.

Plain-English Definition: A company that checks and forwards electronic health claims between providers and insurers.
Example: A clinic sends all claims through a clearinghouse.

Plain-English Definition: A LexisNexis database report of past auto and home claims used by insurers when underwriting.
Example: An insurer sees a prior water claim on a house's CLUE report.
US Notes: Consumers can get a free copy yearly under the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

Plain-English Definition: The federal agency that runs Medicare, works with states on Medicaid and oversees parts of the ACA.
Example: CMS approves Medicare Advantage plans.

Plain-English Definition: The standard claim form (and its electronic 837P equivalent) used by doctors and other professionals to bill health plans.
Example: A clinic submits an 837P electronic claim.

Plain-English Definition: A federal law letting you keep your employer group health coverage for a time after leaving a job, usually paying the full premium plus 2%.
Example: You keep your plan for 18 months after being laid off.
US Notes: Applies to employers with 20+ employees; many states have 'mini-COBRA' laws for smaller employers.

Plain-English Definition: Your share of the cost of a covered service as a percentage, after the deductible is met.
Example: With 20% coinsurance on a $1,000 bill, you pay $200.
US Notes: Not the same as the property coinsurance clause.

Plain-English Definition: A property policy rule that reduces your claim payment if you insure for less than a set percentage (often 80%) of the property's value.
Example: Insuring a $1M building for $600,000 with an 80% clause means a claim is paid at 600/800 of the loss.

Plain-English Definition: Reinsurance fully backed by cash or securities held in trust, often from capital market investors.
Example: A fund posts $100M collateral to back a reinsurance limit.

Plain-English Definition: Pays for damage to your car from hitting another car or object, or from rolling over.
Example: Your car hits a pole; collision pays after the deductible.
US Notes: Optional by law, but usually required by lenders.

Plain-English Definition: Loss ratio plus expense ratio. Under 100% means an underwriting profit; over 100% means an underwriting loss.
Example: A 60% loss ratio plus 35% expense ratio equals 95%.

Plain-English Definition: One limit covering bodily injury and property damage together per accident.
Example: A $500,000 CSL for all liability from one crash.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for vehicles used for business, covering liability and physical damage.
Example: A plumber's work van.

Plain-English Definition: Business insurance covering injuries to others, damage to their property, and personal and advertising injury caused by the business.
Example: A customer slips in your store; CGL pays.
US Notes: ISO form CG 00 01 is the standard occurrence form.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for businesses and organizations.
Example: General liability and workers' comp are commercial lines.

Plain-English Definition: A policy combining two or more commercial coverage parts, like property, GL and inland marine.
Example: A manufacturer's CPP includes property, GL and crime.

Plain-English Definition: Covers a business's buildings, equipment, inventory and other property.
Example: A bakery's ovens and building damaged by fire.

Plain-English Definition: Payment to an agent or broker, usually a percentage of premium, for selling a policy.
Example: A 15% commission on a $2,000 policy is $300.

Plain-English Definition: Charging everyone in an area the same base premium, regardless of health; ACA allows adjustments only for age, location, tobacco and family size.
Example: Two 40-year-olds in the same area pay the same regardless of health.

Plain-English Definition: A rule that reduces the money you can recover by the percentage you were at fault.
Example: You are 20% at fault in a crash with $10,000 of damage, so you recover $8,000.
US Notes: Most states use pure or modified comparative negligence; a few use contributory negligence.

Plain-English Definition: Software that lets agents enter data once and get quotes from multiple insurers.
Example: An independent agent runs one rater for 8 carriers.

Plain-English Definition: Money awarded to repay actual losses, such as medical bills, lost wages and pain and suffering.
Example: An injured worker gets $50,000 for medical bills and lost pay.

Plain-English Definition: A state-created workers' comp insurer that competes with private insurers, often as a market of last resort.
Example: California's State Compensation Insurance Fund.

Plain-English Definition: Pays for damage to your car from causes other than collision, like theft, hail, fire, flood or hitting an animal.
Example: Hail dents your car; comprehensive pays.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance required by law, such as auto liability or workers' compensation.
Example: Your state requires 25/50/25 auto liability.

Plain-English Definition: Deliberately hiding a material fact from the insurer.
Example: Not mentioning a prior home fire when asked about past losses.

Plain-English Definition: When two or more causes, one covered and one excluded, combine to cause a loss.
Example: Wind (covered) and storm surge (excluded) both damage a house.

Plain-English Definition: Something that must happen before the insurer has to pay.
Example: Submitting a proof of loss is a condition precedent to payment.

Plain-English Definition: A contract where the insurer's duty to pay depends on the insured meeting certain conditions, like reporting claims promptly.
Example: Failing to report a loss in time can let the insurer deny payment.

Plain-English Definition: A renewal offered with changed terms, such as higher deductible or reduced coverage.
Example: The insurer renews but raises your wind deductible to 2%.
US Notes: Many states require advance written notice of conditional renewal.

Plain-English Definition: The rules and duties both you and the insurer must follow for the policy to work, such as reporting claims promptly.
Example: You must notify the insurer 'as soon as practicable' after a loss.

Plain-English Definition: The policy bought by a condo association to cover common areas and often the building structure.
Example: The HOA master policy covers the roof and hallways.
US Notes: Florida and other states set condo association insurance requirements.

Plain-English Definition: How a building is built, such as frame, masonry or fire-resistive, which affects fire risk.
Example: A frame (wood) house costs more to insure than a masonry one.
US Notes: ISO uses construction classes 1 through 6.

Plain-English Definition: When repairing or recovering property would cost more than it is worth, so it's treated as a total loss.
Example: A sunk ship that would cost more to raise than it's worth.

Plain-English Definition: A formal complaint by a policyholder to the state insurance department about an insurer or agent.
Example: You complain that your claim hasn't been paid in 60 days.
US Notes: The NAIC publishes complaint indexes by insurer.

Plain-English Definition: The period, usually the first two years, during which the insurer can investigate and contest a life policy for misstatements.
Example: A death in year one triggers a review of the application.

Plain-English Definition: The person who receives the benefit if the primary beneficiary has died or can't receive it.
Example: Your children are contingent beneficiaries.

Plain-English Definition: Covers lost income caused by damage at a key supplier's or customer's property.
Example: Your main supplier's factory burns and you can't produce.

Plain-English Definition: Extra commission paid to an agent based on the profitability or volume of the business they place.
Example: An agency earns a bonus because its loss ratio was below 50%.
US Notes: Some states require disclosure of contingent commissions.

Plain-English Definition: Continuing group health coverage after it would otherwise end, such as through COBRA or state law.
Example: Your spouse continues coverage after divorce.

Plain-English Definition: Latin for 'against the offeror'. Unclear wording in a contract is interpreted against the party who wrote it, usually the insurer.
Example: A court reads an unclear exclusion in the policyholder's favor.
US Notes: US courts widely apply this rule because policies are usually drafted by insurers.

Plain-English Definition: A take-it-or-leave-it contract written by one party. Insurance policies are usually treated this way, so unclear wording favors the insured.
Example: You can't negotiate the wording of your standard auto policy.

Plain-English Definition: Inland marine coverage for mobile tools and heavy equipment wherever they are.
Example: A stolen excavator from a job site is covered.

Plain-English Definition: Liability you take on by agreeing in a contract to cover someone else's legal responsibility.
Example: A lease makes you responsible for injuries in the building.

Plain-English Definition: When more than one policy covers the same loss, the insurers share the cost instead of paying twice.
Example: Two home policies each covering a painting split a $5,000 theft loss.

Plain-English Definition: An older rule that bars you from recovering anything if you were even slightly at fault.
Example: A plaintiff 5% at fault gets nothing under contributory negligence.
US Notes: Still used in a handful of jurisdictions (e.g., Alabama, Maryland, North Carolina, Virginia and D.C.).

Plain-English Definition: The right to convert group coverage to an individual policy without proving good health.
Example: After leaving your job, you convert group life to individual whole life within 31 days.

Plain-English Definition: A term policy that lets you switch to permanent insurance without new medical exams.
Example: You convert your term policy to whole life after a cancer diagnosis.

Plain-English Definition: A condition requiring you to help the insurer investigate and defend claims.
Example: You must attend depositions in a lawsuit your insurer is defending.

Plain-English Definition: Rules that decide which plan pays first when you are covered by more than one plan, so total payments don't exceed the bill.
Example: Your plan pays first and your spouse's plan pays some of what is left.
US Notes: NAIC model rules are used by states; Medicare has its own secondary payer rules.

Plain-English Definition: A fixed amount you pay for a covered service, like a doctor visit or prescription.
Example: A $25 copay for each doctor visit.
Where You'll See It: Insurance ID card, Explanation of benefits, Policy document

Plain-English Definition: The four key factors used to underwrite property: construction, occupancy, protection and exposure.
Example: A brick building with sprinklers near a fire station scores well on COPE.

Plain-English Definition: An insurer's main operational systems: policy administration, billing and claims.
Example: Replacing core systems is a multi-year project.

Plain-English Definition: The monthly charge deducted from a universal life policy's cash value to pay for the death benefit, rising with age.
Example: COI charges increase every year as you age.

Plain-English Definition: The part of health care costs you pay yourself through deductibles, copays and coinsurance.
Example: Your cost sharing for the year totaled $2,300.

Plain-English Definition: Extra savings for lower-income people on silver marketplace plans that lower deductibles and copays.
Example: A CSR silver plan with a $500 deductible instead of $5,000.

Plain-English Definition: The protection a policy provides against specified losses.
Example: Your policy has coverage for theft but not for flood.

Plain-English Definition: A code systems use to identify a particular coverage in data and integrations.
Example: Code 'COLL' for collision coverage.

Plain-English Definition: A section of a commercial package policy for one type of coverage, like property or general liability.
Example: A package policy includes a property coverage part and a GL coverage part.

Plain-English Definition: Confirming that a policy was in force and covers the type of loss reported.
Example: The adjuster verifies the policy was active on the date of the accident.

Plain-English Definition: Numbers on a business auto policy that define which vehicles are covered, like symbol 1 (any auto).
Example: Symbol 1 liability covers any auto used in the business.
US Notes: ISO Business Auto form uses symbols 1–9 and 19.

Plain-English Definition: A company authorized by a Lloyd's managing agent to bind insurance on its behalf.
Example: A US MGA acting as a Lloyd's coverholder.

Plain-English Definition: Codes that describe medical procedures and services on claims, maintained by the American Medical Association.
Example: 99213 is a common office visit code.

Plain-English Definition: How much weight actuaries give to a particular set of data, based on its size and reliability.
Example: A small insurer's own data gets 30% credibility; industry data gets 70%.

Plain-English Definition: Rules letting a ceding insurer reduce its liabilities for reinsurance, often requiring collateral from unauthorized reinsurers.
Example: A cedent holds a letter of credit from an offshore reinsurer.
US Notes: Based on NAIC credit for reinsurance model laws.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays a loan or credit card balance if the borrower dies, becomes disabled or loses a job.
Example: Credit life pays off a car loan after the borrower's death.
US Notes: Regulated by state credit insurance laws.

Plain-English Definition: A score built from your credit report that predicts insurance losses, used in pricing in many states.
Example: A strong insurance score lowers your auto premium.
US Notes: Banned or restricted in some states, e.g., California, Hawaii and Massachusetts for auto.

Plain-English Definition: Covers loss of money, securities and property from crimes like employee theft, forgery, robbery and computer fraud.
Example: A bookkeeper embezzles $200,000.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance paying a lump sum if you're diagnosed with a covered serious illness like cancer, heart attack or stroke.
Example: You receive $20,000 after a cancer diagnosis.
US Notes: Considered an 'excepted benefit' under federal law.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance protecting farmers against crop losses from weather, pests or low prices.
Example: A drought cuts corn yields and the policy pays.

Plain-English Definition: Private insurance covering crops against hail and sometimes fire, not federally subsidized.
Example: Hail shreds a tobacco crop.

Plain-English Definition: A website or app where policyholders view policies, pay bills, get ID cards and file claims.
Example: You download your auto ID card from the portal.

Plain-English Definition: A clause letting the policyholder collect directly from the reinsurer if the ceding insurer becomes insolvent.
Example: A lender requires a cut-through on a small insurer's policy.

Plain-English Definition: Covers costs of data breaches, ransomware and other cyber events, including notification, recovery, extortion and liability.
Example: After ransomware, the policy pays forensics, restoration and legal costs.
US Notes: All states have data breach notification laws that drive cyber costs.

Plain-English Definition: Money a court awards to someone who has been harmed.
Example: A jury awards $200,000 in damages to an injured customer.

Plain-English Definition: A request by a regulator for specific data from insurers.
Example: A state asks all insurers for wildfire non-renewal counts.

Plain-English Definition: Latin for 'about minimal things'. Something too small to matter.
Example: A $2 premium adjustment may be waived as de minimis.

Plain-English Definition: The amount paid to beneficiaries when the insured person dies.
Example: A $250,000 death benefit paid to your spouse.

Plain-English Definition: The summary page of your policy showing who is insured, what is covered, limits, deductibles, premium and policy dates.
Example: Your auto dec page lists your cars, drivers, coverages and six-month premium.

Plain-English Definition: A decision by the insurer not to offer coverage or not to pay a claim.
Example: An applicant with multiple DUIs is declined.
US Notes: Some states require written reasons for declining certain personal lines applicants.

Plain-English Definition: Term insurance where the death benefit gets smaller over time, often to match a mortgage balance.
Example: Coverage falls as your mortgage is paid down.

Plain-English Definition: The amount of a covered loss you pay yourself before the insurer starts paying.
Example: A $500 deductible on a $3,000 car repair means you pay $500 and the insurer pays $2,500.
Where You'll See It: Declarations page, Policy document, Claim documents, Explanation of benefits
US Notes: Health plans often have separate individual and family deductibles; hurricane deductibles in coastal states are often a percentage of the home's insured value.

Plain-English Definition: Legal fees and costs of defending a claim.
Example: $80,000 in attorney fees spent defending a lawsuit.

Plain-English Definition: Defense costs are paid in addition to the policy limit.
Example: A CGL policy pays defense costs on top of the $1M limit.

Also Known As: Burning Limits; Eroding Limits; Wasting Policy
Plain-English Definition: Defense costs reduce the policy limit, leaving less money to pay a settlement.
Example: $300,000 of legal fees reduces a $1M D&O limit to $700,000.
US Notes: Some states restrict defense-within-limits for certain lines.

Plain-English Definition: Under GAAP, acquisition costs spread over the life of the policy instead of expensed at once.
Example: A life insurer amortizes DAC over 20 years.

Plain-English Definition: An annuity that grows tax-deferred for years before income payments begin.
Example: You fund a deferred annuity at 50 and take income at 65.

Plain-English Definition: The section that explains the exact meaning of key words used in the policy. Defined words are often shown in bold or quotes.
Example: The policy defines 'your covered auto' to mean vehicles listed on the declarations.

Plain-English Definition: Data from MGAs and coverholders about policies and claims written under delegated authority.
Example: A carrier builds a pipeline to ingest MGA data.

Plain-English Definition: When a mutual insurer converts to a stock company owned by shareholders.
Example: Policyholders receive shares when their mutual demutualizes.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for dental care, often paying 100% for preventive, 80% for basic and 50% for major services.
Example: Two free cleanings per year plus 50% of a crown.

Plain-English Definition: Cyber coverage for lost income when a key technology vendor suffers an outage or attack.
Example: A cloud provider's outage stops your online store.

Plain-English Definition: A premium paid at the start based on estimated exposures, later adjusted.
Example: A $50,000 deposit premium later adjusted to $55,000.

Plain-English Definition: The loss in value of property over time due to age, wear and obsolescence.
Example: A 10-year-old roof has lost much of its value to depreciation.

Plain-English Definition: An adjuster who handles claims by phone, email and photos without visiting the scene.
Example: A small windshield claim handled entirely by a desk adjuster.

Plain-English Definition: Selling insurance through websites, apps and APIs instead of in-person agents.
Example: A customer buys renters insurance entirely on a phone.

Plain-English Definition: A requirement that a broker first try admitted insurers (often three declinations) before placing in surplus lines.
Example: A broker documents three admitted carriers declined the risk.
US Notes: Details vary by state; some states have 'export lists' that waive it.

Plain-English Definition: The loss in a car's resale value after it has been in an accident, even when fully repaired.
Example: A repaired luxury car is worth $3,000 less due to its accident history.
US Notes: Third-party diminished value claims are recognized in most states; first-party claims mainly in Georgia.

Plain-English Definition: The insurer bills and collects premium directly from the policyholder and pays commission to the agent.
Example: You pay your auto premium straight to the insurer.

Plain-English Definition: Actual physical damage to or loss of property, which is usually required before a property policy pays.
Example: A fire burning your store is direct physical loss; losing customers due to a recession is not.
US Notes: Many COVID-19 business interruption suits turned on this phrase.

Plain-English Definition: A network of body shops approved by an insurer to repair cars with streamlined claims handling.
Example: You take your car to a DRP shop and the insurer pays it directly.
US Notes: Most states let consumers choose their own repair shop.

Plain-English Definition: An insurer that sells directly to customers through its own employees, website or call centers instead of independent agents.
Example: GEICO sells auto insurance online and by phone.

Plain-English Definition: Premium written by the insurer on its own policies, before reinsurance and excluding reinsurance it assumes.
Example: State-level market share tables use direct written premium.

Plain-English Definition: Covers directors and officers against claims alleging wrongful acts in managing the company, and the company itself in some cases.
Example: Shareholders sue the board over a failed merger.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that replaces part of your income if illness or injury keeps you from working.
Example: Pays 60% of salary while you recover from back surgery.

Plain-English Definition: Ways to settle disagreements between insurer and insured, such as appraisal, mediation, arbitration or court.
Example: A claim dispute is resolved through mediation.

Plain-English Definition: Software that produces policy documents, notices and letters by merging data into templates.
Example: Declarations pages are generated at issuance.

Plain-English Definition: The state where an insurer is incorporated, whose regulator is its primary financial supervisor.
Example: An insurer domiciled in Ohio is licensed in 45 states.

Plain-English Definition: State laws making businesses that serve alcohol liable for harm caused by intoxicated customers.
Example: A bar that over-served a customer is sued.
US Notes: Rules differ by state; some states have no dram shop liability.

Plain-English Definition: Points added for accidents and violations that raise auto premiums.
Example: An at-fault accident adds a 3-year surcharge.
US Notes: Some states regulate insurer surcharge plans.

Plain-English Definition: Liability and hull coverage for unmanned aircraft.
Example: A drone crashes into a car during filming.

Plain-English Definition: When an umbrella or excess policy steps in to act as primary coverage because underlying limits are used up or don't cover a loss.
Example: An umbrella drops down to cover a claim excluded by the primary GL.

Plain-English Definition: Levels in a formulary with different cost sharing, such as generic, preferred brand and specialty.
Example: Tier 1 generics cost $10; tier 4 specialty drugs cost 30%.

Plain-English Definition: People who qualify for both Medicare and Medicaid.
Example: A low-income 70-year-old gets both programs.
US Notes: Special Needs Plans (D-SNPs) serve this group.

Plain-English Definition: A software platform for P&C insurers covering policy, billing, claims and rating.
Example: A carrier uses Duck Creek Rating.

Also Known As: Duties in the Event of Loss
Plain-English Definition: Things you must do after a loss, like notifying the insurer, protecting property from more damage and providing records.
Example: After a burst pipe you must stop the water and keep receipts.

Plain-English Definition: A legal obligation to act reasonably to avoid harming others.
Example: A doctor owes patients a duty of care.

Plain-English Definition: Your obligation to tell the insurer about important facts when applying for or renewing insurance.
Example: You must disclose a recent heart surgery on a life insurance application.
US Notes: In the US the duty is usually limited to answering the application's questions truthfully, except in marine insurance.

Plain-English Definition: The insurer's obligation to provide and pay for a lawyer to defend you against a covered lawsuit.
Example: Your insurer hires a lawyer when a customer sues your business.
US Notes: Most states say the duty to defend is broader than the duty to indemnify.

Plain-English Definition: The insurer's obligation to pay judgments or settlements for covered claims.
Example: The insurer pays a $300,000 settlement.

Plain-English Definition: The part of a home policy that covers the house structure itself.
Example: Coverage A of $350,000 for the house.

Plain-English Definition: A property policy for homes, often rentals, that doesn't include the full homeowners package.
Example: A landlord insures a rental house on a DP-3.

Plain-English Definition: The part of the premium that corresponds to time that has already passed on the policy.
Example: After 3 months on a $1,200 annual policy, $300 is earned.

Plain-English Definition: Excludes damage from earthquakes, landslides, sinkholes and similar ground movement.
Example: A crack from an earthquake is excluded unless you bought earthquake coverage.
US Notes: Florida requires insurers to offer sinkhole coverage and cover catastrophic ground cover collapse.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for damage from earthquakes, usually sold separately with a high percentage deductible.
Example: A 15% deductible earthquake policy.
US Notes: In California it is often bought from the California Earthquake Authority (CEA).

Plain-English Definition: The HIPAA standard electronic format for enrolling members in health plans.
Example: An employer sends a weekly 834 enrollment file.

Plain-English Definition: The HIPAA standard electronic format for health plan payment and remittance information sent to providers.
Example: A hospital auto-posts payments from 835 files.

Plain-English Definition: The HIPAA standard electronic format for submitting health care claims.
Example: A clearinghouse transmits 837 files to insurers.

Plain-English Definition: The date and time coverage begins.
Example: Your policy is effective at 12:01 a.m. on March 1.

Plain-English Definition: Recording when each version of policy data became true, so systems can show the policy as of any date.
Example: A query shows which drivers were on the policy last March.

Plain-English Definition: A document showing a building's elevation compared to expected flood levels.
Example: An EC shows the house is 2 feet above base flood elevation.

Plain-English Definition: The number of days you must be disabled or need care before a disability or long-term care policy starts paying.
Example: A 90-day elimination period on a long-term disability policy.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance offered at the point of sale inside another company's product or purchase flow.
Example: Buying trip insurance while booking a flight.

Plain-English Definition: Covers transport to an adequate medical facility or home in a medical emergency while traveling.
Example: An air ambulance from a remote island.

Plain-English Definition: Crime coverage for theft by employees.
Example: A cashier steals from the register over months.

Plain-English Definition: An ACA rule requiring employers with 50 or more full-time employees to offer affordable coverage or pay a penalty.
Example: A 60-employee company must offer health coverage.

Plain-English Definition: Health coverage offered by an employer to employees and families, usually with shared premium costs.
Example: Your employer pays 75% of your health premium.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for lawsuits by employees for work injuries not covered by workers' comp, bundled with WC policies.
Example: A spouse sues for loss of companionship after a worker's injury.

Plain-English Definition: Covers employers against claims by employees of discrimination, harassment, wrongful termination and similar issues.
Example: A former employee sues for wrongful termination.

Plain-English Definition: A written change added to a policy that adds, removes or changes coverage.
Example: Adding an endorsement for water backup coverage to a home policy.
US Notes: Endorsement forms usually must be filed with the state department of insurance.

Plain-English Definition: A policy that pays the face amount at a set date if you are alive, or at death if earlier. Also when a whole life policy's cash value equals the death benefit at maturity age.
Example: A policy endows at age 121.
US Notes: Pure endowment products are rare in the US because of tax rules.

Plain-English Definition: A covered loss that follows from an excluded cause.
Example: Faulty wiring (excluded) causes a fire (covered); the fire damage is an ensuing loss.

Plain-English Definition: States that the policy plus the attached application make up the whole agreement; nothing outside them counts.
Example: An agent's verbal promise isn't part of the contract.

Plain-English Definition: Covers cleanup costs and liability for pollution, which standard liability policies exclude.
Example: A gas station's leaking tank contaminates groundwater.

Plain-English Definition: A plan that covers only in-network care (except emergencies) but usually doesn't require referrals.
Example: You can see an in-network specialist directly.

Plain-English Definition: Covers sudden breakdown of equipment like boilers, HVAC, electrical systems and machinery.
Example: A factory's compressor motor burns out.
US Notes: Boiler inspections are required by many states.

Plain-English Definition: A 1974 federal law that sets standards for most private employer benefit plans, including health and life plans.
Example: An ERISA plan must follow federal appeal procedures.

Plain-English Definition: The rule that ERISA overrides many state laws for employer plans, especially self-funded ones.
Example: A state mandate doesn't apply to a self-funded plan.

Plain-English Definition: Covers professionals against claims that mistakes or negligence in their services caused a client financial loss.
Example: An architect's design error causes costly rework.

Plain-English Definition: Ten categories of services ACA plans must cover, like emergency care, hospitalization, maternity, mental health and prescription drugs.
Example: Your individual plan covers maternity care.
US Notes: Each state picks a benchmark plan defining EHB details.

Plain-English Definition: A written calculation of what it will cost to repair damage.
Example: A body shop estimate of $3,200.

Plain-English Definition: A rule preventing a party from denying something it earlier led someone else to rely on.
Example: An agent told you a loss was covered, so the insurer may be estopped from denying it.

Plain-English Definition: Covers lost costs and revenue if an event is cancelled, postponed or disrupted by covered causes.
Example: A festival cancelled by a hurricane.

Plain-English Definition: A document proving property insurance, often requested by lenders.
Example: A mortgage lender asks for evidence of property insurance.

Plain-English Definition: A payment made by the insurer as a goodwill gesture even though it is not legally required.
Example: An insurer pays $500 ex gratia for a borderline claim to keep a long-time customer happy.

Plain-English Definition: A formal interview where the insured answers the insurer's questions under oath about a claim.
Example: An insurer suspects fraud and requests an EUO.

Plain-English Definition: The chance that losses will exceed a certain amount in a year.
Example: A 1% exceedance probability corresponds to a 100-year loss.

Plain-English Definition: Types of coverage such as dental, vision, hospital indemnity or AD&D that are exempt from many ACA rules.
Example: A standalone dental plan is an excepted benefit.

Plain-English Definition: Wording that gives back coverage that an exclusion would otherwise remove.
Example: Mold is excluded, except when it results from a covered water leak.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays only after another policy's limits are used up.
Example: A $5M excess policy sits above a $1M primary policy.

Plain-English Definition: Reinsurance that pays when a loss exceeds the insurer's retention, up to a limit.
Example: $10M xs $5M: reinsurer pays losses between $5M and $15M.

Plain-English Definition: A judgment above the policy limit that the insurer may have to pay if it acted in bad faith.
Example: A $1M verdict on a $100,000 policy after the insurer refused to settle.

Plain-English Definition: A court judgment larger than the defendant's insurance limits; very large ones ($10M+) are often called nuclear verdicts.
Example: A trucking crash leads to a $50M verdict.

Plain-English Definition: A person specifically listed as not covered when driving your car.
Example: A teen with DUIs is excluded to keep premiums down.
US Notes: Not allowed in some states.

Plain-English Definition: A part of the policy that lists what is NOT covered.
Example: Most home policies exclude flood and earthquake damage.

Plain-English Definition: The part of each non-qualified annuity payment that is a tax-free return of your original investment.
Example: 60% of each payment is tax-free.

Plain-English Definition: The rule that workers' comp is an injured employee's only remedy against the employer, barring most lawsuits.
Example: An injured worker can't sue the employer for negligence.

Plain-English Definition: The amount added to the pure premium to cover expenses, taxes and profit.
Example: A $300 pure premium with a 30% expense load.

Plain-English Definition: Underwriting expenses (commissions, salaries, overhead) divided by premium.
Example: $30M expenses on $100M premium is 30%.

Plain-English Definition: A number that raises or lowers a workers' compensation premium based on the employer's claims history; 1.00 is average.
Example: A mod of 0.85 gives a 15% discount.
US Notes: Calculated by NCCI in most states and by independent bureaus in states like California, New York and Pennsylvania.

Plain-English Definition: Adjusting premium based on the insured's own past loss experience compared with the average.
Example: A company with fewer claims than average gets a lower workers' comp premium.

Plain-English Definition: The date and time coverage ends unless renewed.
Example: Your policy expires on March 1 next year.

Plain-English Definition: A statement from the health insurer showing what a provider billed, what the plan paid and what you owe. It is not a bill.
Example: An EOB shows $800 billed, $500 allowed, $400 paid, you owe $100.

Plain-English Definition: The thing or measure the insurer uses to gauge how much risk it is taking on, such as number of cars, payroll or square footage.
Example: A workers' comp premium is based on payroll per $100 as the exposure.

Plain-English Definition: Tracking and analyzing where insured values are concentrated to manage catastrophe risk.
Example: Mapping all insured homes within 1 mile of the coast.

Plain-English Definition: Extends business income coverage after repairs are done while revenue recovers.
Example: 90 extra days while customers return.

Plain-English Definition: Pays above your dwelling limit, often 25%–50% more, if rebuild costs are higher than expected.
Example: A $400,000 limit with 25% extended pays up to $500,000.

Plain-English Definition: Extra time after a claims-made policy ends to report claims for incidents that happened while it was active.
Example: A retiring doctor buys a tail so later malpractice suits are covered.

Plain-English Definition: A nonforfeiture option that uses cash value to buy term insurance for the full face amount for as long as it lasts.
Example: Cash value buys 12 years of term cover.

Plain-English Definition: A contract to repair or replace a product after the manufacturer's warranty ends; often not legally insurance.
Example: A 3-year plan on a new laptop.
US Notes: Regulated under state service contract laws, not always insurance law.

Plain-English Definition: Review of a denied health claim by an independent organization, after internal appeals, whose decision the plan must follow.
Example: An independent reviewer overturns a denied cancer treatment.
US Notes: Guaranteed by the ACA; run by states or the federal process.

Plain-English Definition: Extra costs to keep operating or reduce downtime after covered damage.
Example: Renting a temporary office after a fire.

Plain-English Definition: Amounts an insurer must pay beyond the policy's terms, often because of bad faith findings.
Example: A court awards $2M against an insurer for mishandling a claim.

Plain-English Definition: The amount of death benefit stated on the policy.
Example: A policy with a face amount of $1,000,000.

Plain-English Definition: Reinsurance arranged for a single, specific policy, negotiated individually.
Example: A large skyscraper is reinsured on a facultative basis.

Plain-English Definition: A federal law governing consumer reports like credit, CLUE and MIB, including notice when they cause adverse action.
Example: You get an adverse action notice after a credit-based higher premium.

Plain-English Definition: The price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller for property.
Example: The FMV of your used car is its typical sale price in your area.

Also Known As: Fair Access to Insurance Requirements Plan
Plain-English Definition: A state-mandated pool that provides basic property insurance to owners who can't get it in the regular market.
Example: A California homeowner in a wildfire zone buys from the California FAIR Plan.
US Notes: Exists in about 30 states and D.C.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for rent you lose when a part of your home you rent out becomes uninhabitable after a covered loss.
Example: You lose $1,000/month from a basement apartment after a fire.

Plain-English Definition: A package policy covering a farm's home, buildings, equipment and liability.
Example: A farmowners policy covers the barn, tractor and farmhouse.

Plain-English Definition: Federal insurance protecting bank deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category.
Example: Your savings are protected when a bank fails.

Plain-English Definition: The government corporation that finances and reinsures the federal crop insurance program, managed by RMA.
Example: FCIC reinsures private crop insurers under the Standard Reinsurance Agreement.

Plain-English Definition: A payment model where providers are paid for each service they perform.
Example: A doctor bills for each visit and test.

Plain-English Definition: The federal agency that responds to disasters and runs the NFIP.
Example: FEMA provides disaster grants after a hurricane.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage protecting against losses from dishonest acts of employees; ERISA requires one for people handling plan funds.
Example: A 401(k) plan's ERISA bond.

Plain-English Definition: Covers people who manage employee benefit plans against claims of mismanagement.
Example: Employees sue over high 401(k) fees.

Plain-English Definition: An adjuster who visits the loss location to inspect damage.
Example: A field adjuster measures fire damage at your house.

Plain-English Definition: Rates can be used after being filed, without waiting for approval, though the regulator can later reject them.
Example: An insurer files new rates and uses them 30 days later.

Plain-English Definition: Small whole life policies, often $5,000–$25,000, meant to pay funeral costs.
Example: A 70-year-old buys $10,000 to cover funeral costs.

Plain-English Definition: A periodic regulatory audit of an insurer's financial condition, usually every 3–5 years.
Example: The domiciliary state examines an insurer's reserves.

Plain-English Definition: State laws requiring drivers to prove they can pay for damage they cause, usually by carrying auto insurance.
Example: Driving without insurance can suspend your license.

Plain-English Definition: An independent opinion on an insurer's ability to pay claims, from agencies like AM Best, S&P and Moody's.
Example: A lender requires an insurer rated A- or better by AM Best.

Plain-English Definition: Covers art and collectibles, usually on an agreed value basis.
Example: A painting damaged in transit to a gallery.

Plain-English Definition: A multi-year insurance contract that transfers limited risk and focuses on spreading loss costs over time.
Example: A company's losses are funded over five years with limited risk transfer.

Plain-English Definition: The first report to the insurer that a loss has happened, which starts the claim process.
Example: You report a car accident through the insurer's app.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays you directly for your own losses.
Example: Collision coverage on your car pays to repair your own car.

Plain-English Definition: An annuity that credits a guaranteed interest rate.
Example: A 5-year fixed annuity paying 5%.

Plain-English Definition: An annuity whose interest is linked to a market index with a floor protecting against losses.
Example: Interest linked to S&P 500 with a 9% cap and 0% floor.
US Notes: Regulated as insurance under state law, not as a security.

Plain-English Definition: Cancelling a policy as of its start date so that no premium is charged.
Example: A policy bound in error is flat cancelled.

Plain-English Definition: An extra premium per $1,000 of coverage charged for a specific risk, like a dangerous hobby.
Example: A pilot pays an extra $2.50 per $1,000 of coverage.

Plain-English Definition: An employer account where you set aside pre-tax money for medical costs; unused money is usually lost at year-end.
Example: You put $1,500 in an FSA for glasses and copays.

Plain-English Definition: Money an insurer holds between collecting premiums and paying claims, which it can invest.
Example: Long-tail liability lines generate large float.

Plain-English Definition: Excludes damage from flooding, surface water, waves and similar water.
Example: River overflow damaging your basement is not covered by standard home insurance.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance covering damage from flooding, which standard home policies exclude.
Example: NFIP coverage pays to repair a flooded ground floor.

Plain-English Definition: An area mapped by FEMA by flood risk; high-risk zones start with A or V.
Example: A home in Zone AE must carry flood insurance if it has a federally backed mortgage.

Plain-English Definition: The minimum interest credited to an indexed product, often 0%, so you don't lose money when the index falls.
Example: The index falls 20%; you're credited 0%.

Plain-English Definition: A state-run fund providing reinsurance to Florida residential property insurers for hurricane losses.
Example: Florida insurers must buy FHCF coverage.

Plain-English Definition: An excess policy that adopts the same terms and conditions as the policy underneath it.
Example: A follow-form excess D&O policy covers what the primary covers.

Plain-English Definition: A principle that the reinsurer must accept the ceding insurer's good-faith claim decisions.
Example: The reinsurer pays its share of a claim the cedent settled reasonably.

Plain-English Definition: A contract clause freeing parties from their obligations when extraordinary events beyond their control occur.
Example: A concert can't go ahead due to a government lockdown, triggering a force majeure clause.
US Notes: Mostly found in commercial contracts; insurance policies rely on their own perils and exclusions.

Plain-English Definition: A standard printed document that makes up part of a policy, identified by a form number.
Example: The ISO homeowners form HO 00 03.
Where You'll See It: Policy document, Declarations page, Policy administration system
US Notes: Most forms must be filed with and approved by state regulators.

Plain-English Definition: A filing required for approval before anyone acquires control of a domestic insurer.
Example: A private equity firm files Form A to buy a life insurer.

Plain-English Definition: Submitting policy forms and endorsements to a state regulator for review.
Example: A new cyber endorsement filed in 48 states.

Plain-English Definition: The unique identifier and edition date printed on each policy form, e.g., 'HO 00 03 05 11'.
Example: The edition date tells which version applies.

Plain-English Definition: A list on the policy of all the form and endorsement numbers that make up the contract.
Example: The dec page lists 'CG 00 01 04 13; CG 21 47 12 07'.

Plain-English Definition: The list of prescription drugs a health plan covers.
Example: Your brand-name drug is not on the formulary, but a generic is.

Plain-English Definition: A nonprofit membership organization that provides life insurance and other benefits to members.
Example: Knights of Columbus offers life insurance to members.

Plain-English Definition: A short period after receiving a policy when you can cancel it for a full refund.
Example: You have 10 days to review your new life policy and cancel for a full refund.
US Notes: Length is set by state law, often 10–30 days; longer for replacements and seniors.

Plain-English Definition: Lets you withdraw a portion, often 10% a year, from an annuity without surrender charges.
Example: You take out 10% in year 3 without penalty.

Plain-English Definition: How often losses or claims happen, usually measured per exposure.
