Example: 5 claims per 100 cars per year is a frequency of 5%.

Plain-English Definition: A licensed insurer issues a policy but passes most or all of the risk to a reinsurer or captive.
Example: A captive can't issue policies in all states, so a fronting carrier issues them and reinsures to the captive.

Plain-English Definition: A premium, or portion of it, that is not refunded if the policy is cancelled.
Example: Event cancellation premium is fully earned at inception.

Plain-English Definition: A health plan where the employer pays premiums to an insurer, which takes on the claims risk.
Example: A small business buys a fully insured group plan.
US Notes: Subject to state insurance mandates.

Plain-English Definition: Standard US accounting rules used for financial reports to investors.
Example: Public insurers report GAAP earnings to the SEC.

Plain-English Definition: Pays the difference between your car's actual cash value and what you still owe on the loan or lease after a total loss.
Example: Your car is worth $20,000 but you owe $24,000; gap pays $4,000.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for auto businesses such as repair shops and dealers, including customers' cars in their care (garagekeepers).
Example: A customer's car is damaged in a shop fire.

Plain-English Definition: Where a vehicle is usually kept overnight, used to set the rating territory.
Example: Listing a cheaper rural address falsely is misrepresentation.

Plain-English Definition: A maritime rule where all parties in a sea voyage share losses from a deliberate sacrifice made to save the voyage.
Example: Cargo is thrown overboard to save the ship; all cargo owners share the loss.

Plain-English Definition: Damages for harm that has no exact price, like pain, suffering and loss of enjoyment of life.
Example: A crash victim receives $30,000 for pain and suffering.

Plain-English Definition: An agreement where a bond principal (and often its owners) promise to repay the surety for any losses.
Example: A contractor's owners personally sign the GIA.

Plain-English Definition: The accounting system recording all financial transactions, fed by policy, billing and claims systems.
Example: Premium and claim payments post to the general ledger.

Plain-English Definition: Broad term for insurance covering a business's legal liability for injuries and property damage to others.
Example: A contractor buys general liability to win jobs.

Plain-English Definition: A statistical technique widely used in insurance pricing to estimate how each rating factor affects losses.
Example: A GLM shows young drivers have 2.5x the claim frequency.
US Notes: Regulators often review GLMs in rate filings.

Plain-English Definition: Converting an address into latitude and longitude for risk and pricing analysis.
Example: A home is geocoded to measure distance to the coast.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for windshield and window damage, sometimes with no deductible.
Example: A cracked windshield is replaced for free.
US Notes: Some states (e.g., Florida, Kentucky, South Carolina) require zero-deductible windshield coverage.

Plain-English Definition: A discount for drivers with no recent accidents or violations.
Example: A 20% discount for 5 clean years.
US Notes: California law mandates a 20% good driver discount.

Plain-English Definition: Extra time after a premium due date during which coverage stays in force before the policy lapses.
Example: A life policy gives a 31-day grace period.
US Notes: ACA marketplace enrollees receiving subsidies get a 3-month grace period; life policies typically have 30–31 days by state law.

Plain-English Definition: A benefit that is limited (often to premiums plus interest) if death from illness occurs in the first two or three years.
Example: Death in year one returns premiums plus 10%.

Plain-English Definition: A 1999 federal law that, among other things, requires financial institutions including insurers to protect customer personal information and give privacy notices.
Example: An insurer mails an annual privacy notice.
US Notes: States enforce GLBA privacy rules for insurers.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance covering a group of people, like employees or members, under one contract.
Example: An employer's group health plan.

Plain-English Definition: Life insurance provided to a group, typically employees, under one master policy.
Example: Your employer provides life cover equal to 1x salary.

Plain-English Definition: A rider allowing you to buy more coverage at set dates or life events without proving good health.
Example: You add $50,000 after your child is born.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage that must be offered regardless of health.
Example: A guaranteed issue final expense policy with a two-year graded benefit.
US Notes: The ACA made major medical guaranteed issue; Medigap has guaranteed issue rights in certain situations.

Plain-English Definition: An optional annuity rider guaranteeing income or withdrawals regardless of market performance.
Example: A GLWB guarantees 5% a year for life.

Plain-English Definition: An annuity feature guaranteeing heirs at least a minimum amount, like premiums paid, at death.
Example: Heirs receive $100,000 even though the account fell to $80,000.

Plain-English Definition: Pays the full cost to rebuild your home even if it exceeds the policy limit.
Example: Rebuild costs $600,000 on a $450,000 limit, all paid.
US Notes: Few insurers still offer it.

Plain-English Definition: Universal life focused on a guaranteed death benefit to a certain age with little cash value.
Example: A GUL guaranteed to age 100.

Plain-English Definition: A state fund that pays claims, up to limits, when an admitted insurer becomes insolvent.
Example: After an insurer fails, the state guaranty association pays your claim up to $300,000.
US Notes: Separate associations for life/health and P&C in each state; limits vary.

Plain-English Definition: A widely used software platform for P&C insurers (PolicyCenter, BillingCenter, ClaimCenter).
Example: An insurer migrates to Guidewire Cloud.

Plain-English Definition: Planning or inventing a loss on purpose to collect insurance.
Example: Burning your own house for the payout.

Plain-English Definition: A period when insurance is harder to get, prices rise and terms tighten.
Example: Commercial property rates rose sharply in the 2020–2023 hard market.

Plain-English Definition: A condition that makes a loss more likely or more severe.
Example: Storing oily rags in a garage is a hazard that raises the chance of fire.

Plain-English Definition: A coding system for supplies, equipment, drugs and services, including CPT as Level I.
Example: A HCPCS code for a wheelchair.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays for medical care such as doctor visits, hospital stays and prescriptions.
Example: Your employer plan pays most of a $20,000 surgery.

Plain-English Definition: The government-run service where individuals and small businesses shop for ACA health plans and apply for subsidies.
Example: You buy a silver plan on HealthCare.gov.
US Notes: Some states run their own exchanges (e.g., Covered California).

Plain-English Definition: An employer-funded account that reimburses employees for medical costs or individual insurance premiums.
Example: An employer gives $400 a month via ICHRA to buy an individual plan.

Plain-English Definition: A tax-advantaged savings account for medical costs, available with a high-deductible health plan.
Example: You put $3,000 pre-tax into an HSA and use it for doctor bills.
US Notes: IRS sets yearly contribution limits.

Plain-English Definition: A coding system that groups diagnoses to estimate how costly a patient will be, used for risk adjustment.
Example: Coding diabetes with complications raises a member's risk score.

Plain-English Definition: A plan with a higher deductible that meets IRS rules, allowing you to open an HSA.
Example: A plan with a $3,300 deductible and HSA eligibility.

Also Known As: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
Plain-English Definition: A 1996 federal law that protects the privacy and security of health information and limits certain health plan exclusions.
Example: A health insurer must encrypt member medical data.

Plain-English Definition: Covers a business's liability for rented vehicles and employees' personal cars used for work.
Example: An employee crashes their own car driving to a client.

Plain-English Definition: A health plan that usually covers only in-network care and requires a primary care doctor and referrals for specialists.
Example: You need a referral from your PCP to see a dermatologist.

Plain-English Definition: The most common US homeowners form: open perils on the house, named perils on belongings.
Example: Most homeowners buy an HO-3.
US Notes: Based on ISO form HO 00 03.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for renters covering belongings, liability and additional living expense, but not the building.
Example: A renter's $20,000 policy for furniture and electronics.

Plain-English Definition: A homeowners form that covers both the house and belongings on an open perils basis.
Example: A higher-end homeowner buys HO-5.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for condo owners covering their unit's interior, belongings and liability.
Example: Covers new kitchen cabinets after a fire in your condo unit.

Plain-English Definition: A homeowners form for older homes whose market value is below rebuild cost, usually paying repair with common materials or ACV.
Example: A 1900s house with plaster walls insured under HO-8.

Plain-English Definition: A contract where one party agrees to protect the other from claims or losses.
Example: A subcontractor agrees to hold the general contractor harmless for injuries on site.
US Notes: Many states have anti-indemnity statutes limiting these in construction.

Plain-English Definition: A package policy covering your house, belongings and personal liability.
Example: An HO-3 policy covering a single-family home.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays a fixed amount per day you're in the hospital, regardless of actual costs.
Example: $200 per day for a 5-day hospital stay.

Plain-English Definition: A clause defining how long a period (e.g., 72 hours) counts as one catastrophe event.
Example: Wind losses within 72 hours count as one hurricane event.

Plain-English Definition: Physical damage insurance on a ship or aircraft itself.
Example: A ship's engine room fire is covered.

Plain-English Definition: A special, usually percentage-based, deductible that applies to hurricane damage.
Example: A 5% hurricane deductible applies when a named storm damages your Florida home.
US Notes: Used in about 19 coastal states and D.C.; each state sets its own trigger rules.

Plain-English Definition: A life insurance or annuity product combined with long-term care benefits.
Example: A single-premium policy that pays LTC or a death benefit.

Plain-English Definition: A reserve for claims that have happened but haven't yet been reported to the insurer.
Example: A December accident reported in February is part of year-end IBNR.

Plain-English Definition: The code set used to record diagnoses on health claims.
Example: E11.9 is the code for type 2 diabetes without complications.
US Notes: US uses ICD-10-CM (diagnoses) and ICD-10-PCS (inpatient procedures).

Plain-English Definition: Covers costs of restoring your identity after theft, like legal fees and lost wages.
Example: Pays costs to fix accounts opened in your name.

Plain-English Definition: An annuity bought with a lump sum that starts paying income within a year.
Example: A retiree buys a SPIA for $200,000.

Plain-English Definition: A policy that is currently active and providing coverage.
Example: Your policy is in force until next March.

Plain-English Definition: Doctors, hospitals and other providers that have a contract with your health plan to charge agreed rates.
Example: An in-network visit costs you a $20 copay.
Where You'll See It: Insurance ID card, Explanation of benefits

Plain-English Definition: After a set time (usually two years), the insurer can't cancel or deny a life policy for misstatements on the application, except in some cases like fraud.
Example: After two years, a small error on your life application can't be used to deny the claim.
US Notes: Required by state law for life policies; generally 2 years.

Plain-English Definition: International trade terms (like FOB and CIF) that define when risk passes from seller to buyer and who buys insurance.
Example: Under CIF, the seller must insure the goods.

Plain-English Definition: Losses paid plus change in reserves during a period.
Example: Paid $40M, reserves up $10M, incurred $50M.

Plain-English Definition: The idea that insurance should put you back in the same financial position you were in before the loss, not make you better off.
Example: After a $10,000 fire loss you receive $10,000, not $15,000.

Plain-English Definition: An adjuster hired by an insurer on contract rather than employed by it, often used after catastrophes.
Example: Hundreds of IAs deploy to Florida after a hurricane.

Plain-English Definition: An agent who represents several insurers and can shop for the best fit.
Example: An independent agent compares quotes from six carriers.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays based on an index like area yield or rainfall rather than an individual's loss.
Example: A rancher gets paid when the pasture rainfall index falls below normal.

Plain-English Definition: Universal life where cash value interest is linked to a stock market index, with a floor and cap.
Example: Credited interest follows the S&P 500 up to a 10% cap, with a 0% floor.
US Notes: NAIC Actuarial Guideline 49-A limits illustrated rates.

Plain-English Definition: A rough, non-binding price estimate given before full underwriting.
Example: A broker gets an indication of about $40,000 for a D&O policy.

Plain-English Definition: An ACA rule requiring most people to have health coverage; the federal penalty was reduced to $0 from 2019.
Example: No federal tax penalty for being uninsured since 2019.
US Notes: California, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Rhode Island and D.C. have their own mandates with penalties.

Plain-English Definition: A reinsurance contract that pays when total industry losses from an event exceed a set amount.
Example: Pays if a US hurricane causes industry losses over $30B.

Plain-English Definition: Damage caused by a natural quality of the item itself, not an outside event. It is usually excluded.
Example: Fruit rotting in transit because of its own ripening is inherent vice.

Plain-English Definition: Covers property that moves or is in transit over land, or unusual property like equipment, bridges and fine art.
Example: A contractor's tools and equipment covered at job sites.
US Notes: NAIC's Nationwide Marine Definition sets what qualifies.

Plain-English Definition: An insured who didn't take part in a wrongful act, such as arson by a spouse, and may still recover.
Example: A wife whose husband set fire to their home may still be paid for her share.
US Notes: Many states protect innocent co-insureds by statute, especially in domestic violence cases.

Plain-English Definition: When an insurer cannot pay its debts, including claims.
Example: A Florida homeowners insurer becomes insolvent after hurricanes.

Plain-English Definition: A visit to evaluate a property or operation for hazards before or after issuing coverage.
Example: An inspector photographs a home's roof for underwriting.

Plain-English Definition: Covers materials and equipment being installed until the job is accepted.
Example: HVAC units in transit and during install.

Plain-English Definition: Paying the premium in parts, such as monthly or quarterly, sometimes with a fee.
Example: A $1,200 policy paid in 12 installments of $100 plus $5 fee.

Plain-English Definition: Standard London-market cargo wordings: (A) broadest all-risks, (B) and (C) named perils.
Example: A shipper buys ICC (A) cover.
US Notes: Widely used in US cargo placements; American Institute forms also exist.

Plain-English Definition: You can only insure something if you would suffer a financial loss if it were damaged, destroyed or lost.
Example: You can insure your own house, but not your neighbor's house.
US Notes: In life insurance, insurable interest must exist when the policy is bought; state laws address stranger-originated life insurance (STOLI).

Plain-English Definition: A risk that insurers are willing and able to cover because losses are accidental, measurable and not catastrophic for everyone at once.
Example: House fire is insurable; a stock market crash is not.

Plain-English Definition: An arrangement where you pay a company a fee so that it covers the cost of certain losses if they happen. Many people pay in, and the money pays for the few who suffer a loss.
Example: You pay $1,200 a year for home insurance; when a pipe bursts, the insurer pays $8,000 for repairs.
US Notes: Insurance is regulated mainly by the states, not the federal government.

Plain-English Definition: The official who heads a state's insurance regulator.
Example: The California Insurance Commissioner is elected.
US Notes: Elected in some states, appointed in most.

Plain-English Definition: An NAIC model law requiring insurers and agents to have information security programs and report cybersecurity events.
Example: An insurer notifies the regulator of a data breach within 72 hours.
US Notes: Adopted by roughly half the states; New York has its own cyber rule (23 NYCRR 500).

Plain-English Definition: A central database that combines policy, claims and billing data for reporting and analytics.
Example: Actuaries pull loss triangles from the warehouse.

Plain-English Definition: Deliberately lying or deceiving to get insurance money or lower premiums.
Example: Staging a car crash to claim injuries is insurance fraud.
US Notes: Most states have fraud bureaus and require insurers to report suspected fraud.

Plain-English Definition: A parent company that owns one or more insurers; transactions between affiliates are regulated.
Example: A holding company owns five P&C insurers in different states.

Plain-English Definition: A card showing proof of coverage, like an auto ID card or health member card.
Example: You show your auto ID card to police.
US Notes: Most states now accept digital auto ID cards.

Plain-English Definition: The written contract that spells out what is covered, what is not, and the duties of both sides.
Example: Your 40-page homeowners policy document.

Plain-English Definition: How close the insured amount is to the true replacement cost of the property.
Example: An underwriter checks ITV to make sure the $500,000 limit matches rebuild cost.

Plain-English Definition: Financial instruments whose value depends on insurance losses, like cat bonds and collateralized reinsurance.
Example: A pension fund invests in ILS for diversification.

Plain-English Definition: The person or organization protected by the policy.
Example: On a car policy, you and family members who drive your car are insureds.

Plain-English Definition: The person whose life is covered; their death triggers the payout. They may differ from the policyowner.
Example: A company insures the life of its CEO.

Plain-English Definition: Excludes claims brought by one insured against another, such as the company suing its own directors.
Example: The company sues its former CFO; the D&O excludes it.

Plain-English Definition: The company that issues the policy and agrees to pay covered claims.
Example: State Farm or a small regional mutual is an insurer.

Plain-English Definition: The part of the policy stating what the insurer promises to cover.
Example: 'We will pay those sums the insured becomes legally obligated to pay as damages because of bodily injury...'

Plain-English Definition: Technology-driven companies or innovations in insurance, such as app-based insurers, data tools or digital distribution.
Example: An app that quotes renters insurance in 90 seconds.

Plain-English Definition: Excludes injury or damage the insured intended or expected to cause.
Example: Punching someone is not covered by your homeowners liability.

Plain-English Definition: A process where insurers resolve subrogation disputes between themselves without going to court.
Example: Two auto insurers resolve fault through Arbitration Forums, Inc.

Plain-English Definition: Money an insurer earns by investing premiums and reserves before claims are paid.
Example: Interest from bonds held to back reserves.

Plain-English Definition: A beneficiary who cannot be changed without their consent.
Example: A divorce decree requires an ex-spouse to be irrevocable beneficiary.

Plain-English Definition: An advisory organization (part of Verisk) that writes standard policy forms, collects statistics and files loss costs.
Example: The standard CGL form CG 00 01 is an ISO form.

Plain-English Definition: Creating and delivering the formal policy documents after coverage is bound.
Example: The policy is issued and emailed as a PDF.

Plain-English Definition: The insured's age when the policy is issued, used to price premiums.
Example: A policy issued at 35 is priced at issue age 35.

Plain-English Definition: Inland marine coverage for jewelry retailers' and wholesalers' stock.
Example: A jewelry store robbery.

Plain-English Definition: A policy covering two people that pays when the first one dies.
Example: Business partners buy first-to-die coverage.

Plain-English Definition: A federal law letting injured seamen sue their employers for negligence.
Example: A deckhand sues the vessel owner after a fall.

Plain-English Definition: Life or disability insurance a business buys on an important employee, with the business as beneficiary.
Example: A startup insures its founder for $2M.
US Notes: Employer-owned policies must meet IRS notice and consent rules (Section 101(j)).

Plain-English Definition: Covers ransom payments, crisis consultants and related costs if an insured person is kidnapped.
Example: An executive traveling abroad is kidnapped.

Plain-English Definition: Checks to verify the identity of customers, used to prevent money laundering and fraud.
Example: An insurer verifies ID before issuing a large annuity.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for owners who rent out property, covering the building, liability and lost rent.
Example: A landlord's policy pays lost rent after a fire.

Plain-English Definition: When a policy ends because the premium was not paid within the grace period.
Example: Your life policy lapses after missing payments.

Plain-English Definition: The share of policies that stop because premiums are not paid.
Example: A 5% annual lapse rate on term policies.

Plain-English Definition: The larger the group of similar risks, the more accurately an insurer can predict how many losses will occur.
Example: An insurer covering 100,000 cars can predict accident numbers far better than one covering 100.

Plain-English Definition: A slice of coverage between two amounts, often insured by different insurers in a tower.
Example: One insurer takes the $5M excess of $5M layer.

Plain-English Definition: Collecting information about potential customers and selling or passing it to agents or insurers.
Example: An agent buys internet leads for Medicare supplement shoppers.
US Notes: Telemarketing and TCPA rules affect lead use.

Plain-English Definition: An older system, often mainframe-based, still running critical insurance operations.
Example: A 1980s COBOL policy system still issues life policies.

Plain-English Definition: A condition that limits when and how you can sue the insurer, such as within two years of the loss.
Example: You must sue within one year after the loss.
US Notes: Limits must meet state minimums.

Plain-English Definition: Term life where the premium and death benefit stay the same for the whole term.
Example: A 30-year level term policy at $40 a month.

Plain-English Definition: A self-funded plan for smaller employers with fixed monthly payments covering expected claims, admin and stop-loss.
Example: A 40-employee firm pays a steady monthly amount and may get a refund if claims are low.

Plain-English Definition: Legal responsibility to pay for harm you cause to someone else or their property.
Example: If your dog bites a visitor, you may have liability for their medical bills.

Plain-English Definition: If the insurer broadens a form without extra charge, the broader coverage automatically applies to your current policy.
Example: A new edition adds coverage mid-term and it applies to you immediately.

Plain-English Definition: A bond required by a government to obtain a license, guaranteeing compliance with laws.
Example: An auto dealer must post a $50,000 bond.

Plain-English Definition: A lender or leasing company with a financial interest in the insured property.
Example: The car finance company is the lienholder.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays money to your beneficiaries when you die.
Example: A $500,000 policy pays your family if you die.

Plain-English Definition: Payments continue for the annuitant's life and stop at death, with nothing to heirs.
Example: Payments stop when the annuitant dies.

Plain-English Definition: Selling a life insurance policy to a third party for more than its cash surrender value but less than its death benefit.
Example: A 78-year-old sells a $1M policy for $200,000.
US Notes: Regulated by most states; rescission periods apply.

Also Known As: Limit; Limit of Insurance; Policy Limit
Plain-English Definition: The most the insurer will pay for a covered loss or during the policy period.
Example: A liability policy with a $1,000,000 limit will not pay more than $1 million for a lawsuit.

Plain-English Definition: The amount of a risk an insurer or reinsurer accepts; also a share of a risk taken by a market.
Example: A syndicate writes a 10% line on a cargo policy.

Plain-English Definition: A category of insurance, like personal auto, homeowners or workers' comp, used for products, reporting and regulation.
Example: Reporting premiums by LOB on the annual statement.
US Notes: NAIC annual statement lines define regulatory LOBs.

Plain-English Definition: The types of insurance a producer's license allows them to sell, such as life, health, property or casualty.
Example: A producer with P&C lines of authority can't sell life insurance.

Plain-English Definition: Covers businesses that sell or serve alcohol against claims from intoxicated customers causing harm.
Example: A bar is sued after a drunk patron crashes.

Plain-English Definition: A claim that has become a lawsuit.
Example: A slip-and-fall claim goes to litigation.

Plain-English Definition: An order to keep all records related to a claim or lawsuit and not delete them.
Example: The IT team preserves emails for a pending bad faith suit.

Plain-English Definition: Covers death of livestock from accidents, disease or other causes; federal price-risk livestock plans also exist.
Example: A prize bull dies from lightning.

Plain-English Definition: A London insurance marketplace where syndicates underwrite risks; it's a major non-admitted market in the US.
Example: A US film production insurance placed at Lloyd's.
US Notes: Lloyd's writes US business mainly as a surplus lines insurer and reinsurer; it's admitted only in Illinois, Kentucky and the US Virgin Islands.

Plain-English Definition: A line where claims take many years to be reported and settled, like liability and workers' comp.
Example: Asbestos claims appeared decades after exposure.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays for help with daily activities in a nursing home, assisted living or at home.
Example: Pays $200 a day for a nursing home.
US Notes: Many states have LTC partnership programs linked to Medicaid asset protection.

Plain-English Definition: A rider allowing death benefit to be used for long-term care costs.
Example: The rider pays $4,000 a month toward assisted living.

Plain-English Definition: Disability insurance that pays for a long period, often to age 65, after a waiting period.
Example: Pays 60% of salary for years after a disabling stroke.

Plain-English Definition: The reduction in value or financial harm that triggers a claim, such as damage, injury or death.
Example: A tree falling on your garage is a loss.

Plain-English Definition: The process of investigating, evaluating and settling a claim.
Example: The loss adjustment took three weeks.

Plain-English Definition: The costs of investigating and settling claims, separate from the claim payments themselves.
Example: Adjuster fees and legal costs are LAE.

Plain-English Definition: Pays your share of a special assessment charged by an HOA for a covered loss to common property.
Example: The HOA charges each owner $3,000 after a lobby fire.

Plain-English Definition: Services and actions to reduce the frequency or severity of losses.
Example: A loss control engineer recommends machine guards at a factory.

Plain-English Definition: The part of the premium needed just to pay expected losses, before expenses and profit.
Example: Expected losses of $300 per car per year is the loss cost.
US Notes: In many states, advisory organizations like ISO file loss costs that insurers adjust with their own expenses.

Plain-English Definition: The pattern of how total losses for a period grow as more claims are reported and paid.
Example: Liability losses may take 10 years to fully develop.

Plain-English Definition: A multiplier showing how much losses are expected to grow from one evaluation age to the next or to ultimate.
Example: A 12-to-24 month LDF of 1.40.

Plain-English Definition: A table showing losses by accident year across successive evaluation dates, used to project final losses.
Example: Rows are accident years; columns are 12, 24, 36 months.

Plain-English Definition: A record of past claims used to judge the likelihood of future losses.
Example: Three water claims in five years raise your home premium.

Also Known As: Additional Living Expense; ALE; Coverage D
Plain-English Definition: Coverage for extra costs of living elsewhere while your home is being repaired after a covered loss.
Example: The policy pays for a hotel while your fire-damaged house is fixed.

Plain-English Definition: A party, often a lender, that is paid from the claim along with or instead of the insured.
Example: The bank financing your car is a loss payee.

Plain-English Definition: Losses (usually including loss adjustment expenses) divided by earned premium.
Example: $60M losses on $100M earned premium is a 60% loss ratio.

Plain-English Definition: A range of loss ratio in which a reinsurer does not pay, so the cedent keeps those losses.
Example: Losses between 70% and 80% loss ratio stay with the cedent.

Plain-English Definition: Money set aside for claims that have happened but aren't paid yet, including unreported ones.
Example: An insurer holds $500M in loss reserves.

Applies To Lines: Property, Casualty/Liability, Motor, Commercial, Financial Lines
Plain-English Definition: A report from an insurer listing the claims a policyholder has had over a period.
Example: A business gives five years of loss runs to a new insurer.
US Notes: Several states require insurers to provide loss runs within a set time of request.

Plain-English Definition: The expected rate at which claim costs grow over time due to inflation and other factors.
Example: A 6% annual severity trend for auto liability.

Plain-English Definition: Any insurance plan where the cost depends on the insured's own losses, such as retro plans or large deductibles.
Example: A large-deductible workers' comp program for a trucking company.

Plain-English Definition: A package of D&O, EPLI, fiduciary and crime coverages for private companies or nonprofits.
Example: A nonprofit buys a management liability package.

Plain-English Definition: A firm given authority by insurers to underwrite, bind, issue policies and sometimes handle claims on their behalf.
Example: An MGA writes pet insurance backed by a large carrier.
US Notes: MGAs are regulated under state MGA laws based on an NAIC model act.

Plain-English Definition: A term similar to MGA, stressing underwriting authority delegated by insurers.
Example: An MGU specializes in cyber risks for small firms.

Plain-English Definition: A regulatory review of how an insurer treats customers in sales, underwriting, claims and complaints.
Example: A state exam finds late claim payments and fines the insurer.

Plain-English Definition: An adjustment to an annuity's surrender value based on interest rate changes since purchase.
Example: Rates rose, so the MVA lowers your surrender value.

Plain-English Definition: Lawsuits by many people harmed by the same product or action.
Example: Thousands sue over a harmful chemical.

Plain-English Definition: The single contract issued to an employer or organization for group insurance.
Example: The employer holds the master policy; employees get certificates.

Plain-English Definition: A fact that would affect whether an insurer accepts a risk or what premium it charges.
Example: Having had two DUIs is a material fact for auto insurance.

Plain-English Definition: The date a policy or annuity ends and pays its value, if the insured is alive.
Example: A policy matures at age 121.

Plain-English Definition: The largest loss that could happen at a location if all protection systems failed.
Example: The MFL assumes the sprinklers fail and the whole warehouse burns.

Plain-English Definition: A 1945 federal law leaving insurance regulation mainly to the states and giving insurers limited antitrust exemption.
Example: Why each state regulates its own insurance market.

Plain-English Definition: A federally required endorsement guaranteeing a trucking company's liability limits are available to the public.
Example: The insurer pays a victim under MCS-90 even if the policy wouldn't otherwise apply.

Plain-English Definition: Covers claims of defamation, copyright infringement and invasion of privacy from published content.
Example: A publisher is sued for libel.

Plain-English Definition: A joint federal-state program providing health coverage to people with low income and some other groups.
Example: A low-income family gets free coverage through Medicaid.
US Notes: Eligibility and benefits vary by state; not all states expanded Medicaid under the ACA.

Plain-English Definition: Medicaid benefits delivered through private health plans that contract with the state.
Example: A state pays an MCO a monthly amount per member.

Plain-English Definition: The share of health premiums spent on medical care and quality improvement.
Example: A plan spends 82 cents of each premium dollar on care.
US Notes: The ACA requires 80% MLR for individual and small group, 85% for large group, or rebates are paid.

Plain-English Definition: Professional liability for doctors, nurses and health facilities against claims of patient injury from treatment.
Example: A surgeon is sued for a surgical error.
US Notes: Some states cap non-economic damages in malpractice cases; some have patient compensation funds.

Plain-English Definition: Health care services needed to diagnose or treat an illness under accepted medical standards; plans usually only cover these.
Example: Cosmetic surgery is usually not medically necessary.

Plain-English Definition: Pays medical bills for you and passengers after an accident, regardless of fault, usually in smaller amounts than PIP.
Example: $5,000 MedPay covers an ER visit.

Plain-English Definition: Pays small medical bills for guests injured on your property, regardless of fault.
Example: A neighbor's child falls off your swing; $1,500 medical is paid.

Plain-English Definition: Assessing a person's health to decide whether and at what price to offer life or health coverage.
Example: An applicant with diabetes is rated up.
US Notes: The ACA bans medical underwriting for major medical health insurance.

Plain-English Definition: The federal health insurance program for people 65 and older and some younger people with disabilities.
Example: At 65 you enroll in Medicare Part A and B.

Plain-English Definition: Private health plans approved by Medicare that replace Original Medicare coverage, often with extra benefits and a network.
Example: An MA HMO includes dental and vision.

Plain-English Definition: The yearly period, October 15 to December 7, when Medicare beneficiaries can change Medicare Advantage or Part D plans.
Example: You switch Part D plans during AEP.

Plain-English Definition: The part of Medicare covering inpatient hospital care, skilled nursing, hospice and some home health.
Example: Part A pays for your 3-day hospital stay after your deductible.

Plain-English Definition: The part of Medicare covering doctor visits, outpatient care and preventive services, with a monthly premium.
Example: Part B pays 80% of approved doctor charges.

Plain-English Definition: Medicare prescription drug coverage offered through private plans.
Example: A Part D plan covers your blood pressure pills.
US Notes: The Inflation Reduction Act capped Part D out-of-pocket costs starting 2025.

Plain-English Definition: Private insurance that pays some costs Original Medicare doesn't, like coinsurance and deductibles.
Example: Medigap Plan G covers your 20% Part B coinsurance.
US Notes: Plans are standardized by letter (A–N); Massachusetts, Minnesota and Wisconsin use different standards.

Plain-English Definition: Federal rules requiring mental health and substance use benefits to be no more restrictive than medical benefits.
Example: Therapy visits can't have higher copays than other doctor visits.

Plain-English Definition: ACA plan categories based on how much of costs the plan pays on average: bronze 60%, silver 70%, gold 80%, platinum 90%.
Example: A bronze plan has low premiums but high deductibles.

Plain-English Definition: A US organization where member life and health insurers share coded information from past applications to detect nondisclosure.
Example: MIB shows a prior application disclosing heart problems.
US Notes: Consumers can request their MIB file free under FCRA.

Plain-English Definition: A change made to a policy during its term, which may change the premium.
Example: Adding a teen driver in month 4 increases the premium.

Plain-English Definition: A federal law requiring performance and payment bonds on federal construction contracts over $150,000.
Example: A federal courthouse project requires bonds.
US Notes: States have 'Little Miller Acts' for state projects.

Plain-English Definition: The lowest premium the insurer will charge for a policy regardless of exposures or cancellation.
Example: Even after mid-term cancellation, a $250 minimum premium applies.

Plain-English Definition: A false statement on an application or in a claim.
Example: Saying you don't smoke when you do is a misrepresentation.

Plain-English Definition: If your age was wrong on the application, the benefit is adjusted to what the premium paid would have bought at the correct age.
Example: A benefit is reduced from $100,000 to $92,000 because the insured was older than stated.

Plain-English Definition: A draft law written by the NAIC that states can adopt, sometimes with changes.
Example: The NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law adopted by many states.

Plain-English Definition: A life policy funded too quickly under federal tax rules, which loses some tax advantages on loans and withdrawals.
Example: Paying a huge single premium turns a policy into a MEC.
US Notes: Defined in Internal Revenue Code Section 7702A.

Plain-English Definition: Limits or excludes coverage for mold damage.
Example: Mold from long-term humidity isn't covered.

Plain-English Definition: A state-run workers' comp insurer that is the only allowed source of WC coverage in that state.
Example: Ohio employers must buy WC from the Ohio BWC.

Plain-English Definition: The risk that someone acts dishonestly, such as faking a claim, because they are insured.
Example: A struggling business owner sets fire to the shop to collect insurance.

Plain-English Definition: Carelessness that happens because a person knows they are insured.
Example: Leaving your car unlocked because 'insurance will pay if it's stolen'.

Plain-English Definition: The rate of illness or disability in a group.
Example: Disability insurers price based on morbidity rates.

Plain-English Definition: The chance of dying within a given period, often per 1,000 people at a given age.
Example: A mortality rate of 2 per 1,000 at age 50.

Plain-English Definition: A table showing the probability of death at each age, used to price life insurance and annuities.
Example: The 2017 CSO table is used for reserves.
US Notes: The CSO (Commissioners Standard Ordinary) tables are adopted by the NAIC.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that protects the lender if a borrower stops paying the mortgage, typically required with a down payment under 20%.
Example: You pay PMI until you reach 20% equity.
US Notes: FHA loans use federal mortgage insurance premiums (MIP).

Plain-English Definition: Life insurance meant to pay off a mortgage if the borrower dies.
Example: A decreasing term policy pays the remaining mortgage.

Plain-English Definition: Protects the mortgage lender's interest so it gets paid even if the homeowner's own coverage is voided.
Example: A claim check is made out to you and your mortgage company.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for trucking companies, including liability required by federal rules for interstate haulers.
Example: A trucking firm needs $750,000 minimum liability.
US Notes: FMCSA sets minimum limits for interstate carriers.

Plain-English Definition: Covers freight hauled by a trucker against damage or loss.
Example: A load of TVs is stolen from a trailer.

Plain-English Definition: A state record of a person's driving history, including violations, accidents and suspensions.
Example: An MVR shows two speeding tickets in three years.
US Notes: Obtained from each state DMV; retention periods vary.

Plain-English Definition: Federally subsidized crop insurance covering yield loss from many natural causes.
Example: A soybean farmer is paid after floods.
US Notes: Sold by private Approved Insurance Providers and reinsured by the federal government.

Plain-English Definition: A discount for buying more than one policy, such as home and auto, from the same insurer.
Example: 15% off for bundling home and auto.

Plain-English Definition: An insurer owned by its policyholders rather than shareholders.
Example: State Farm and Northwestern Mutual are mutuals.

Plain-English Definition: The organization of US state insurance regulators that writes model laws and sets accounting and reporting standards.
Example: NAIC model laws guide how states regulate data security.

Plain-English Definition: A standard code classifying businesses by industry, used in underwriting and data.
Example: NAICS 722511 means full-service restaurants.

Plain-English Definition: The person or business specifically listed on the declarations page, who has the main rights and duties under the policy.
Example: 'Jane Smith' is shown as named insured on the declarations page of her home policy.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage only for the causes of loss specifically listed in the policy.
Example: A policy covering fire, lightning, windstorm and hail only.

Plain-English Definition: A plan with a small group of providers, usually in exchange for lower premiums.
Example: A marketplace plan limited to one hospital system.

Plain-English Definition: A federal program run by FEMA that provides flood insurance to property owners in participating communities.
Example: You buy NFIP flood insurance through your agent.
US Notes: Building coverage caps at $250,000 for homes.

Plain-English Definition: A unique ID number assigned to each licensed producer nationwide.
Example: NPN 1234567 appears on appointment filings.

Plain-English Definition: The organization that collects data and files workers' compensation loss costs and class codes in most states.
Example: NCCI calculates an employer's experience mod.
US Notes: Some states, like California and New York, use their own rating bureaus.

Plain-English Definition: Failing to take the care a reasonable person would take, causing harm to someone.
Example: A store that doesn't clean a spill may be negligent if a shopper slips.

Plain-English Definition: The death benefit minus the cash value; what the insurer truly has at risk.
Example: $500,000 death benefit minus $100,000 cash value is $400,000 NAR.

Plain-English Definition: Written premium after subtracting premium paid to reinsurers.
Example: $50M gross minus $10M ceded equals $40M net written.

Plain-English Definition: Rules requiring health plans to have enough providers so members can get care without long travel or waits.
Example: A plan must have a pediatrician within 30 miles.
US Notes: Standards set by states and CMS for marketplace plans.

Plain-English Definition: Covers claims from others harmed by your data breach or security failure.
Example: Customers sue after their card data is stolen.

Plain-English Definition: Policies written for customers who were not previously insured by that insurer.
Example: A spike in new business after a marketing campaign.

Plain-English Definition: Pays to replace a totaled new car with a brand new one instead of its depreciated value.
Example: Your 1-year-old car is replaced with a new model.

Plain-English Definition: A nonprofit that runs a national database and gateway for producer licensing across states.
Example: An agency uses NIPR to renew non-resident licenses in 10 states.

Plain-English Definition: A 2022 federal law protecting patients from surprise bills for most emergency care and some out-of-network care at in-network facilities.
Example: An out-of-network anesthesiologist can't balance bill you after in-network surgery.
US Notes: Many states had their own surprise billing laws before this federal law.

Plain-English Definition: A system where your own insurer pays your injury costs regardless of fault, and lawsuits are limited.
Example: Your own PIP pays after a crash in New York.
US Notes: About a dozen states use no-fault systems.

Plain-English Definition: A promise that a UL policy will stay in force as long as required premiums are paid, even if cash value runs out.
Example: Paying the guarantee premium keeps the policy alive to age 95.

Plain-English Definition: An insurer not licensed in a state but allowed to write coverage there through surplus lines brokers, with more freedom on rates and forms.
Example: A hard-to-place coastal property risk goes to a non-admitted insurer.
US Notes: Not backed by state guaranty funds in most states.

Plain-English Definition: The reinsurer pays losses above a set retention up to a limit; premiums aren't shared in proportion.
Example: The reinsurer pays losses above $5M.

Plain-English Definition: An annuity bought with after-tax money; only the earnings are taxed on withdrawal.
Example: Buying an annuity with savings from your bank account.

Plain-English Definition: The insurer's decision not to continue a policy when it expires.
Example: An insurer non-renews homes in a wildfire zone.
US Notes: States set minimum notice periods (often 30–60 days) and sometimes restrict reasons.

Plain-English Definition: Choices for using cash value if you stop paying premiums: take cash, buy reduced paid-up insurance or extended term.
Example: You choose reduced paid-up insurance of $30,000.
US Notes: Required by state standard nonforfeiture laws.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage on a new claims-made policy for incidents before its start date, replacing the need for a tail from the old policy.
Example: A new insurer grants prior acts back to 2015.

Plain-English Definition: A written notice that a policy will be cancelled on a certain date.
Example: A notice of cancellation for non-payment gives 10 days.
US Notes: Minimum notice periods are set by state law.

Plain-English Definition: Telling the insurer that a loss or claim has happened.
Example: Calling your insurer the day after a car accident.

Plain-English Definition: Excludes losses from nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination.
Example: Contamination from a nuclear plant accident is excluded.
US Notes: Nuclear liability is handled by the Price-Anderson Act and nuclear pools.

Plain-English Definition: The party protected by a surety bond.
Example: The city is the obligee on a road construction bond.

Plain-English Definition: How a building is used, such as owner-occupied home, rental or restaurant.
Example: A restaurant is a different occupancy from an office.

Plain-English Definition: An accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to the same harmful conditions, that causes injury or damage.
Example: A leaking pipe damaging a neighbor's unit over several weeks may be one occurrence.

Plain-English Definition: A policy that covers injury or damage that happens during the policy period, no matter when the claim is made.
Example: A 2020 occurrence policy covers a 2020 injury even if the lawsuit comes in 2025.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for ships, cargo and marine liability for goods moving by sea.
Example: A container of electronics lost overboard.

Plain-English Definition: A US Treasury office whose sanctions rules forbid insurers from dealing with sanctioned people or countries.
Example: A payment is blocked because the claimant is on the sanctions list.

Plain-English Definition: The yearly window when you can sign up for or change health insurance.
Example: ACA open enrollment runs from November 1 to January 15 in most states.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for all causes of loss except those specifically excluded.
Example: An HO-3 covers the dwelling on an open perils basis.

Plain-English Definition: Combined ratio minus the investment income ratio; shows overall operating profitability.
Example: A 102% combined ratio minus 6% investment income ratio gives 96%.

Plain-English Definition: Pays extra costs to rebuild to current building codes after a covered loss.
Example: New code requires sprinklers when rebuilding.

Plain-English Definition: An insurer's internal review of its risks and whether it has enough capital, reported to regulators.
Example: A large insurer files an ORSA summary report yearly.
US Notes: Required by NAIC model for larger insurer groups.

Plain-English Definition: Policy wording explaining how this policy shares a loss with other policies that cover the same thing.
Example: A policy says it pays excess over any other valid insurance.

Plain-English Definition: Covers structures on your property not attached to the house, like fences, sheds and detached garages.
Example: Coverage B pays to rebuild a fence knocked down in a storm.

Plain-English Definition: Providers with no contract with your plan; you usually pay more, or everything.
Example: An out-of-network specialist costs you 50% coinsurance.

Plain-English Definition: The most you'll pay for covered care in a plan year; after that, the plan pays 100%.
Example: After paying $9,000, all covered care is free for the rest of the year.
US Notes: The ACA sets a federal maximum each year for in-network essential health benefits.

Plain-English Definition: A policy change with an effective date earlier than a change already processed, which forces the system to recalculate later changes.
Example: A backdated vehicle addition entered after a later address change.

Plain-English Definition: A commission paid to a managing agent or MGA on business written by agents under it.
Example: An MGA earns a 5% override.

Plain-English Definition: A disability definition that pays if you can't do your specific job, even if you could do another.
Example: A surgeon who can't operate is paid even while teaching.

Plain-English Definition: Claim payments already made.
Example: $3M paid on hurricane claims so far.

Plain-English Definition: Small amounts of extra paid-up whole life coverage bought with dividends or extra premium, increasing cash value and death benefit.
Example: Dividends buy $2,000 of paid-up additions each year.

Plain-English Definition: A basic health exam for a life insurance application, often including blood and urine samples, done by a trained examiner.
Example: A nurse visits your home to take blood pressure and a blood sample.

Applies To Lines: Property, Specialty, Agriculture, Alternative Risk Transfer
Plain-English Definition: Coverage that pays a set amount when a measured event occurs, like wind speed or rainfall, rather than based on actual damage.
Example: A hotel receives $1M automatically when a hurricane with 120 mph winds passes nearby.

Plain-English Definition: Damage that can be repaired and doesn't destroy the whole insured item.
Example: A dented bumper is a partial loss.

Plain-English Definition: A policy eligible for dividends.
Example: A whole life policy from a mutual insurer that pays dividends.

Plain-English Definition: The percentage of the index gain credited to an indexed product.
Example: With 80% participation, a 10% index gain credits 8%.

Plain-English Definition: A partial marine loss that falls only on the owner of the damaged property.
Example: Only one shipper's cargo is damaged by seawater.

Plain-English Definition: A federal index-based program paying ranchers when rainfall in their area falls below normal.
Example: A rancher is paid when rainfall is 60% of normal.

Plain-English Definition: A surety bond guaranteeing that a contractor will pay subcontractors and suppliers.
Example: A supplier is paid by the surety after the contractor defaults.

Plain-English Definition: The way annuity or life benefits are paid, such as life only, period certain or lump sum.
Example: A 'life with 10 years certain' payout.

Plain-English Definition: A federal agency that insures private defined-benefit pension plans.
Example: PBGC pays pensions when a company's plan fails.

Plain-English Definition: Verisk's Property Claim Services unit identifies catastrophes and estimates industry losses in the US; a 'PCS cat' is an event it designates.
Example: A severe hailstorm gets a PCS catastrophe serial number.

Plain-English Definition: Latin for 'by head'. The benefit is shared equally among surviving beneficiaries.
Example: Three surviving children split the benefit equally.

Plain-English Definition: A health plan measure of cost or revenue divided by members per month.
Example: Claims costs of $450 PMPM.

Plain-English Definition: Excess of loss reinsurance that applies to each individual risk.
Example: Protects against a single large factory fire above $2M.

Plain-English Definition: Latin for 'by branch'. If a beneficiary dies first, their share goes to their own descendants.
Example: Your son dies before you; his share goes to his children.

Plain-English Definition: The most the insurer will pay for any single event, no matter how many claims come from it.
Example: A $1M each-occurrence limit caps payment for one warehouse fire even if five people sue.

Plain-English Definition: A deductible set as a percentage of the insured value rather than a flat dollar amount.
Example: A 2% wind deductible on a $300,000 home is $6,000.

Plain-English Definition: A surety bond guaranteeing that a contractor will complete a project according to the contract.
Example: The surety finishes a project after the contractor fails.

Plain-English Definition: A cause of loss, such as fire, wind, theft or flood.
Example: Fire and lightning are perils covered by most home policies.

Plain-English Definition: A payout option guaranteeing payments for a set number of years even if the annuitant dies.
Example: 10-year certain means heirs get payments until year 10.

Plain-English Definition: The time from the damage until the property should reasonably be repaired, during which business income is paid.
Example: Rebuilding takes 5 months, so income is paid for 5 months.

Plain-English Definition: Life insurance that lasts your whole life if premiums are paid and builds cash value.
Example: Whole life and universal life are permanent insurance.

Plain-English Definition: Someone who drives your car with your permission and is generally covered by your policy.
Example: A friend borrows your car and crashes; your policy responds.

Plain-English Definition: The share of policies that remain in force over time; the opposite of lapse.
Example: 13-month persistency of 90%.

Plain-English Definition: Liability for offenses like libel, slander, false arrest, privacy invasion and copying another's advertising idea.
Example: A competitor sues you for defamatory ads.

Plain-English Definition: A policy covering your car and your liability for accidents.
Example: A policy for two cars and three drivers.
US Notes: Most states require minimum liability limits; New Hampshire doesn't mandate insurance for most drivers.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance covers a person, not a thing, so it generally can't be transferred without the insurer's consent.
Example: Selling your car does not transfer your auto policy to the buyer.

Plain-English Definition: Pays medical bills and lost wages for you and passengers regardless of who caused the accident.
Example: PIP pays $10,000 of your medical bills after a crash.
US Notes: Required in no-fault states like Florida, Michigan and New York.

Plain-English Definition: Covers you if you're legally responsible for injuring someone or damaging their property.
Example: A guest trips on your stairs and sues; Coverage E pays.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for individuals and families, such as auto, homeowners and renters.
Example: Home and auto are the biggest personal lines.

Plain-English Definition: Covers your belongings like furniture, clothes and electronics.
Example: Coverage C pays for a stolen laptop.

Plain-English Definition: Covers veterinary bills for pets due to accidents and illness.
Example: Pays 80% of a dog's $4,000 surgery.
US Notes: NAIC Pet Insurance Model Act adopted by several states.

Plain-English Definition: A company that manages prescription drug benefits for health plans, including formularies, pharmacy networks and pricing.
Example: A PBM processes your prescription at the pharmacy counter.
US Notes: Many states have passed PBM transparency laws.

Plain-English Definition: A physical condition that increases the chance or size of a loss.
Example: Old knob-and-tube wiring in a house is a physical hazard.

Plain-English Definition: The 12-month period for health plan benefits, deductibles and out-of-pocket limits.
Example: Your deductible resets on January 1.

Plain-English Definition: The core software an insurer uses to manage policies through quoting, issuing, changes, renewals and cancellations.
Example: Guidewire PolicyCenter or Duck Creek Policy used as PAS.

Plain-English Definition: The yearly date on which the policy began, when many values and premiums change.
Example: Your universal life cost of insurance updates on each policy anniversary.

Plain-English Definition: Giving the policy to the policyholder, which may start the free look period.
Example: An agent delivers a life policy and gets a signed delivery receipt.

Plain-English Definition: A return of part of the premium paid to owners of participating policies when the insurer does well. It is not guaranteed.
Example: A $600 dividend used to buy paid-up additions.

Plain-English Definition: A document projecting how a life policy's premiums, cash values and death benefits may change over time, showing guaranteed and non-guaranteed values.
Example: An illustration shows cash value at age 65 under current and guaranteed rates.
US Notes: Governed by the NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations Model Regulation.

Plain-English Definition: A loan from the insurer using your policy's cash value as security.
Example: You borrow $10,000 from your whole life policy.
US Notes: Unpaid loans reduce the death benefit; loans on MECs may be taxable.

Plain-English Definition: A unique identifier assigned to a policy.
Example: Policy number HO-1234567 on your ID card.

Plain-English Definition: The time span during which the policy is in force, from the effective date to the expiration date.
Example: 12:01 a.m. January 1 to 12:01 a.m. January 1 next year.

Plain-English Definition: Money a life insurer must hold to pay future benefits promised under its policies.
Example: Reserves required under principle-based reserving.

Plain-English Definition: The current state of a policy in the system, such as quoted, bound, in force, cancelled, lapsed or expired.
Example: A policy moves from 'bound' to 'in force' on its effective date.

Plain-English Definition: The geographic area where the policy provides coverage.
Example: A US auto policy covers the US, its territories and Canada.

Plain-English Definition: Grouping of losses and premium by the year the policy started.
Example: Losses on policies written in 2024.

Plain-English Definition: The person or organization that owns the insurance policy and controls it.
Example: A parent owns a life policy on their child; the parent is the policyholder.

Plain-English Definition: An insurer's assets minus liabilities under statutory accounting; the cushion that protects policyholders.
Example: An insurer with $2B surplus can absorb big losses.

Plain-English Definition: An exclusion removing coverage for injury or damage caused by pollutants.
Example: A chemical leak contaminating a river is not covered under a standard CGL.
US Notes: Courts in different states interpret its scope differently.

Plain-English Definition: The right to keep group coverage after leaving the group by paying premiums directly.
Example: You port your group life policy after changing jobs.

Plain-English Definition: A group of policies managed or analyzed together.
Example: An insurer's Florida homeowners portfolio.

Plain-English Definition: Transferring a block of existing liabilities, such as old claims, to another insurer or reinsurer.
Example: An insurer transfers its asbestos reserves to a run-off specialist.

Plain-English Definition: A plan combining HMO and PPO features: a primary doctor and referrals, but some out-of-network coverage.
Example: You pay more to see out-of-network doctors with a referral.

Plain-English Definition: A health plan that lets you see any provider, paying less in-network, without needing referrals.
Example: You see an out-of-network specialist and pay 40% coinsurance.

Plain-English Definition: A health problem you had before your coverage started.
Example: Asthma diagnosed before buying a policy.
US Notes: The ACA bans excluding pre-existing conditions in major medical plans; other products like travel or short-term plans may still exclude them.

Plain-English Definition: A statistical or machine-learning model that uses data to predict outcomes like claims or lapses.
Example: A model predicts which auto claims are likely fraudulent.
US Notes: Some states require filing models used in rating.

Plain-English Definition: The amount you pay the insurer to keep your coverage in force. It can be paid all at once or in installments.
Example: Your auto policy costs $1,500 a year, paid as $125 each month.
US Notes: Premium tax is charged by each state on premiums written there.

Plain-English Definition: A review after the policy ends of the insured's actual exposures, such as payroll or sales, to calculate the final premium.
Example: An audit finds payroll was higher than estimated, so you owe more premium.

Plain-English Definition: A loan from a finance company to pay an insurance premium, repaid in installments.
Example: A contractor finances a $60,000 premium over 10 months.
US Notes: Premium finance companies are licensed by states.

Plain-English Definition: A state tax on insurance premiums written in that state, paid by the insurer.
Example: A 2% premium tax on all policies sold in a state.
US Notes: Rates generally range around 1–4% and differ by state and line.

Plain-English Definition: A federal tax credit that lowers monthly premiums for marketplace plans based on income.
Example: A family pays $150 instead of $900 a month thanks to APTC.

Plain-English Definition: Net written premium divided by policyholders' surplus; a measure of how much risk an insurer takes relative to its capital.
Example: $300M premium on $150M surplus gives 2:1.

Plain-English Definition: Crop insurance payments when weather stops a farmer from planting by the final planting date.
Example: Flooded fields prevent corn planting.

Plain-English Definition: Routine care like screenings, checkups and vaccines to prevent illness, often covered at no cost.
Example: A free annual flu shot and mammogram.
US Notes: The ACA requires in-network preventive services with no cost sharing.

Plain-English Definition: The first person or entity in line to receive the death benefit.
Example: Your spouse is the primary beneficiary.

Plain-English Definition: Your main doctor who provides basic care and, in many plans, coordinates referrals.
Example: You choose a family doctor as your PCP.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance that pays first, before any other policy.
Example: Your auto liability is primary when you drive your own car.

Plain-English Definition: In surety, the party whose performance is guaranteed by the bond.
Example: The contractor is the principal on a performance bond.

Plain-English Definition: A US method of calculating life reserves using company-specific assumptions and scenarios instead of fixed formulas.
Example: An insurer calculates VM-20 reserves for its term portfolio.
US Notes: Adopted through the NAIC Valuation Manual beginning 2017.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for wrongful acts that occurred before the policy's start date, back to the retroactive date.
Example: An E&O policy covers errors made in the last five years.

Plain-English Definition: A rating system where the regulator must approve rates before they can be used.
Example: California requires prior approval for home insurance rates.

Plain-English Definition: Approval the health plan must give before certain services or drugs are covered.
Example: An MRI requires prior authorization.
US Notes: Many states and CMS have added rules to speed up prior authorization decisions.

Plain-English Definition: A notice telling customers what personal information the insurer collects and shares.
Example: A privacy notice arrives with your new policy.

Plain-English Definition: Latin for 'in proportion'. Something is divided or calculated in proportion to time or share.
Example: Cancel a $1,200 annual policy after 3 months and you get $900 back on a pro rata basis.

Plain-English Definition: A cancellation where the refund is exactly proportional to the unused time.
Example: Cancel halfway through a $1,000 policy, get $500 back.
US Notes: Insurer-initiated cancellations are normally pro rata.

Plain-English Definition: An estimate of the largest loss likely from a single event at a given probability.
Example: A 1-in-250-year PML of $1B for earthquake.

Plain-English Definition: The regulatory term for anyone licensed to sell, solicit or negotiate insurance, including agents and brokers.
Example: A state licenses you as a property and casualty producer.
US Notes: Used in the NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act.

Plain-English Definition: A state-issued license that allows a person to sell insurance in specific lines.
Example: You pass the life and health exam to get your license.
US Notes: Non-resident licenses are needed to sell in other states.

Plain-English Definition: Software for defining insurance products (coverages, limits, rules, rates, forms) without custom coding.
Example: A product owner adds a new endorsement in the configurator.

Plain-English Definition: Covers claims that a product you made or sold caused injury or damage.
Example: A defective toaster starts a kitchen fire.

Plain-English Definition: A structured description of an insurance product's coverages, options, limits, deductibles, rules and forms used by systems.
Example: A homeowners product model with 20 coverages and 5 deductible options.

Plain-English Definition: Covers costs of recalling products that are defective or contaminated.
Example: A food maker recalls peanut butter due to salmonella.

Plain-English Definition: Liability for injury or damage caused by your products or finished work after it leaves your control.
Example: A deck you built collapses a year later.

Plain-English Definition: A separate annual aggregate limit for products-completed operations claims under a CGL.
Example: A $2M PCO aggregate separate from the general aggregate.

Plain-English Definition: Coverage for professionals like accountants, lawyers and consultants against claims of negligent services.
Example: A lawyer misses a filing deadline and is sued.

Plain-English Definition: An extra commission paid to the cedent if the reinsured business is profitable.
Example: 20% of profits returned to the ceding company.

Plain-English Definition: A firm that runs an insurance program for a niche class under delegated authority.
Example: A program administrator for youth sports leagues.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance for a specific niche class, like dentists or landscapers, managed by an MGA under a carrier's paper.
Example: A program insuring 5,000 craft breweries.

Plain-English Definition: A state law setting deadlines by which insurers must pay or respond to claims.
Example: A health insurer must pay a clean claim within 30 days.
US Notes: Deadlines vary by state and line.

Also Known As: Sworn Statement in Proof of Loss
Plain-English Definition: A formal, often sworn, statement of the amount and details of your claim.
Example: You sign a proof of loss for $42,000 in fire damage.
US Notes: NFIP flood claims require a proof of loss within 60 days unless extended.

Plain-English Definition: The branch of insurance covering property damage and liability, as opposed to life and health.
Example: Auto and home insurers are P&C insurers.

Plain-English Definition: Physical damage to tangible property, including loss of its use.
Example: Your employee damages a client's floor.

Plain-English Definition: Pays for damage you cause to other people's property.
Example: You hit a fence; PD pays to fix it.

Plain-English Definition: The reinsurer takes an agreed share of premium and losses.
Example: A 50% share of every premium and every loss.

Plain-English Definition: Health information that can identify a person, protected under HIPAA.
Example: A claim with your name and diagnosis is PHI.

Plain-English Definition: Marine liability coverage for shipowners, including crew injury, pollution and collision liabilities, often from mutual P&I clubs.
Example: A P&I club pays for an oil spill cleanup.

Plain-English Definition: A 1 to 10 rating by ISO of a community's fire protection, used in property pricing.
Example: A home in protection class 3 pays less than one in class 9.

Plain-English Definition: The group of doctors, hospitals and other providers a health plan contracts with.
Example: An HMO's network covers local hospitals only.

Plain-English Definition: The main or most direct cause of a loss, used to decide whether the loss is covered.
Example: A storm knocks down a power line that starts a fire; the storm may be treated as the proximate cause.

Plain-English Definition: A licensed adjuster hired by the policyholder, not the insurer, to negotiate a claim for a percentage fee.
Example: A business hires a public adjuster for 10% of the settlement.
US Notes: Licensed and fee-capped by state; some states cap fees after catastrophes.

Plain-English Definition: Extra money a court awards to punish especially bad behavior, not to repay a loss.
Example: A company that knowingly hid a product defect is ordered to pay $5M in punitive damages.
US Notes: Whether insurance may pay punitive damages varies by state; some states prohibit it as against public policy.

Plain-English Definition: A group of similar businesses that buy liability insurance together to get better terms.
Example: A group of daycare centers jointly buying liability insurance.

Plain-English Definition: Expected losses divided by exposures; the amount needed to pay claims only.
Example: Total losses of $1M over 10,000 car-years gives a pure premium of $100.

Plain-English Definition: A risk where only a loss or no loss can happen, with no chance of gain. Only pure risks are normally insurable.
Example: The chance your house burns down is a pure risk.

Plain-English Definition: An annuity funded with pre-tax retirement money such as an IRA or 401(k).
Example: Rolling a 401(k) into an IRA annuity.

Plain-English Definition: A change such as marriage, birth, moving or losing coverage that allows a special enrollment.
Example: Having a baby is a qualifying life event.

Plain-English Definition: A proportional treaty where the reinsurer takes a fixed percentage of every policy's premium and losses.
Example: A 25% quota share cedes one-quarter of all premiums and claims.

Plain-English Definition: An offer from an insurer showing the price and terms at which it would provide coverage.
Example: An online auto quote of $98 per month.

Plain-English Definition: The share of quotes that become bound policies.
Example: 100 quotes, 25 bound: a 25% hit ratio.

Plain-English Definition: Malicious software that locks data until a ransom is paid; cyber policies may cover extortion costs.
Example: A hospital's systems are encrypted and attackers demand bitcoin.
US Notes: OFAC warns payments to sanctioned actors are prohibited.

Plain-English Definition: The price per unit of exposure used to calculate the premium.
Example: A rate of $0.50 per $100 of property value on a $300,000 building gives $1,500.

Plain-English Definition: Whether rates are high enough to cover expected losses, expenses and a reasonable profit.
Example: An actuary finds rates are 8% inadequate.

Plain-English Definition: Submitting proposed rates and rating rules to a state regulator.
Example: An insurer files a 9% auto rate increase in Texas.

Plain-English Definition: The actuarially calculated rate change needed to reach target profitability.
Example: The indication calls for +12%, but the insurer files +7%.

Plain-English Definition: A table of rates or factors looked up by the rating engine, such as factors by age or territory.
Example: A lookup table of territory factors by ZIP code.

Plain-English Definition: A specific set of rates identified by effective date and state, so the system applies the correct rates to each policy.
Example: New business on or after 7/1 uses rate version 2025-07.
US Notes: States may require separate new-business and renewal effective dates.

Plain-English Definition: The step-by-step formula that combines base rates and factors to calculate the premium.
Example: Premium = base rate × territory × age × vehicle × discounts.
US Notes: Filed with state regulators as part of rate filings.

Plain-English Definition: The measure an insurer uses to price a policy, such as payroll, sales, area or units.
Example: General liability for a restaurant may be rated on gross sales.

Plain-English Definition: Software that calculates premiums by applying rates, factors and rules to a risk's details.
Example: A rating engine returns a $1,234 auto premium from 40 inputs.

Plain-English Definition: A characteristic used to adjust the premium, such as age, location or claims history.
Example: Living in a city increases the territory rating factor for auto insurance.
US Notes: Some states ban or limit factors such as credit score, gender or occupation.

Plain-English Definition: A rule in some courts that honors the coverage an ordinary policyholder would reasonably expect, even if the fine print says otherwise.
Example: A court finds a policyholder reasonably expected water damage coverage.
US Notes: Adopted in varying forms by some states only.

Plain-English Definition: Giving a customer part of the commission or something of value to get them to buy a policy.
Example: An agent offers $200 cash back to buy a policy.
US Notes: Illegal or restricted in most states, though many now allow small gifts or value-added services.

Plain-English Definition: A court process where the state regulator takes control of a troubled insurer to fix or wind it down.
Example: A regulator places an insurer in liquidation.

Plain-English Definition: An unincorporated group of members who insure each other, managed by an attorney-in-fact.
Example: USAA and Erie Insurance Exchange are reciprocals.

Plain-English Definition: An interview recorded by the adjuster about how a loss happened.
Example: The adjuster records your account of the crash.

Plain-English Definition: The depreciation amount held back on a replacement cost claim, paid once you actually repair or replace the item.
Example: The insurer pays $6,000 ACV now and the remaining $4,000 after the new roof is installed.

Plain-English Definition: Money the insurer gets back after paying a claim, through subrogation, salvage or reinsurance.
Example: A $4,000 subrogation recovery from another insurer.

Plain-English Definition: A nonforfeiture option that uses cash value to buy a smaller fully paid policy.
Example: Your $100,000 policy becomes $35,000 with no more premiums.

Plain-English Definition: Sending a risk to a senior underwriter or other team for approval because it falls outside normal rules or authority.
Example: The rating engine refers an applicant with three recent claims.

Plain-English Definition: Approval from your primary care doctor to see a specialist, required by some plans.
Example: Your HMO needs a referral before a cardiology visit.

Plain-English Definition: An annuity linked to an index that offers more upside than an FIA but shares losses beyond a buffer.
Example: A 10% buffer absorbs the first 10% of losses.
US Notes: SEC-registered product.

Plain-English Definition: Restoring a lapsed or cancelled policy, sometimes with conditions such as proof of insurability.
Example: You reinstate your life policy within 3 years by paying back premiums and showing good health.

Plain-English Definition: Premium paid to restore a reinsurance limit after it has been used by a loss.
Example: After a hurricane uses the limit, the insurer pays to reinstate it for a second event.

Plain-English Definition: Insurance bought by insurers to protect themselves against large or numerous losses.
Example: A Florida home insurer buys reinsurance for hurricane losses above $50M.
US Notes: US reinsurance is regulated through ceding insurers' credit-for-reinsurance rules.

Plain-English Definition: A broker who arranges reinsurance between insurers and reinsurers.
Example: A broker places a $1B catastrophe program across 30 reinsurers.

Plain-English Definition: The company that accepts risk from an insurer in a reinsurance deal.
Example: Munich Re takes part of a US insurer's catastrophe risk.

Plain-English Definition: A signed document where a claimant gives up further claims in exchange for payment.
Example: An injured driver signs a release after accepting $25,000.
